x: God Almighty says:
h
Praise be to God

who chose Muhammad for his message and selected him to deliver it on his behalf. He sent him to his creation as a prophet and sent him down his book, upright, and made it without any crookedness. What He meant by His statement, upright is balanced and straight. It was said: What He meant by it is that it is balanced over all other books, perfecting them and preserving them. It was mentioned by those who said: What He meant by it is balanced and straight.

c: Ali Bani Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And He has not made therein any crookedness * Straight
, he said: He sent down the Book as justice and straight,
h
and He has not made therein any crookedness
. Ibn Abbas was impressed by his statement with this, along with his explanation of the meaning of straight, that straight is delayed after His statement,
h
and He has not made therein any crookedness
, and its meaning is to bring it forward, meaning: He sent down the Book to His servant as straight.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Zaid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak,
m: regarding his statement, upright, he said: straight.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “And He has not made it crooked. Straight.” That is, straight, with no difference in it. 22858 - Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said:

c: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Has He not made for it any crookedness
? He said: God sent down the Book straight, and did not make for it any crookedness. 22859 - Bishr told us, he said:

c: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Praise be to God

, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made it crooked * [but] straight. He said: And in some readings it is but made it straight. The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is what Ibn Abbas said, and those who said what he said in this regard, because of the evidence of his statement,
h
And He has not made therein any crookedness
, so the Most High informed us that He sent down the Book that He sent down to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, straight, Surat al-Kahf 18:1
h
Praise be to God

, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made therein any crookedness. straight, with no difference or discrepancy in it, rather some of it confirms some of it, and some of it testifies to some of it, with no crookedness in it, and no deviation from the truth. The kasra of the ‘ayn in His statement, crookedness, is because the Arabs say this about every crookedness in religion, or in what is not seen as straight, but is perceived clearly as erect like ivory in religion. That is why the ‘ayn is broken in this place, and likewise crookedness in the road, because it is not an erect person. As for what is crooked in people that are erect, its ‘ayn is opened like crookedness in a canal, a piece of wood, and the like. Ibn Abbas used to say about the meaning of His statement,
h
And He has not made therein any crookedness
: He did not make it ambiguous.

x: Who said that?
22860 - Ali told us, he said:

c: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: And He has not made for it any crookedness * Straight. And He has not made for it any confusion.

x: No, and there is no disagreement among the Arabs that the meaning of his saying standing even if it is delayed is to present it alongside the book. It was said: The Almighty began this Surah by mentioning Himself as He deserves, and by reporting the revelation of His Book to His Messenger, informing the polytheists of Mecca that Muhammad is His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. This is because the polytheists had asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about things that the Jews of Qurayzah and Nadir had taught them, and they had ordered them to ask him about them, and they said: If he tells you about them, then he is a prophet, and if he does not tell you about them, then he is a fabricator. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, promised them an appointment to answer them, but the revelation from him was somewhat delayed, and the arrival of Gabriel, peace be upon him, was delayed from his appointment with the people, so the polytheists said that he had broken his appointment with them, and that he was a fabricator.
So God revealed this Surah as an answer to their questions, and He began its beginning by mentioning Him, and denying the polytheists in the story that they had told among themselves.

Who said that? Abu Kurayb narrated: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: An old man from Egypt, who came forty-something years ago, narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, as narrated by Abu Jaʿfar al-Tabari, who said: Quraysh sent al-Nadr ibn al-Harith and ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt to the Jewish rabbis in Medina, and they said to them: Ask them about Muhammad, describe his characteristics to them, and tell them what he says, for they are the people of the first book, and they have knowledge of what we do not have of the knowledge of the prophets. So they set out until they arrived in Medina, and they asked the Jewish rabbis about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they described to them his affair and some of his sayings, and they said: You are the people of the Torah, and we have come to you so that you may tell us about this companion of ours.

The Jewish rabbis said to them: Ask him about three things that we command you to do, for if he tells you about them, then he is a prophet sent, and if he does not, then the man is a liar, so interpret his opinion according to your opinion! Ask them about the young men who had gone in the first era, what happened to them, for they had a strange story. Ask them about a wandering man who reached the east and west of the earth, what was his story? Ask them about the spirit, what is it? If he tells you about it, then he is a prophet, so follow him. But if he does not tell you, then he is a man who makes up stories, so do with him as you see fit. So Al-Nadr and Uqbah came until they reached Mecca to the Quraysh, and they said: O people of Quraysh, we have come to you with a decision that will decide what is between you and Muhammad. The Jewish rabbis have ordered us to ask him about matters.

c: So they told them
m: about it, so they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, tell us, so they asked him about what they had ordered him to do, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I will tell you tomorrow what you asked about, and he did not make an exception, so they left him, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, remained for fifteen nights, and God did not reveal anything to him about that, and Gabriel, peace be upon him, did not come to him, until the people of Mecca became alarmed and said: Muhammad promised us tomorrow, and today we have become fifteen and he has not informed us of anything that we asked him about, and until the revelation was delayed from him, and he was distressed by what the people of Mecca were saying, then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him, from God Almighty, with Surat Ashab al-Kahf, in which He reproached him for his sadness over them and told him about what they asked him about regarding the matter of the young men and the wandering man, and the words of God Almighty: “And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the affair of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” Ibn Ishaq said: It was reported to me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, opened the surah and said: Praise be to God who sent down to me… His servant, the Book, meaning Muhammad, you are My Messenger, in fulfillment of what they asked about his prophethood, and He has not made it crooked * straight: meaning, moderate, with no difference in it. God Almighty says: He sent down to His servant the Qur’an, moderate and straight, with no crookedness in it, that He may warn you, O people, of a severe punishment from God. By punishment He means immediate torment, present humiliation and force. His statement, from Him means: from God. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ishaq:
m: To warn of a severe punishment means an immediate punishment in this world and a torment in the Hereafter. From Him means from your Lord who sent you as a Messenger.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: something similar.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, from Him: meaning from Him.

x: If someone were to say: Where is the object of his statement, to warn? It was said that its object is omitted, and it was sufficient to indicate what appeared in the speech about it from its mention, and it is an implied connected word that warns before the punishment, as if it was said: to warn you of a punishment, just as it was said: to frighten His allies it is: to frighten you with His allies. And His statement,
h
And He gives good tidings to the believers

, meaning: And He gives good tidings to those who believe in God and His Messenger, who do righteous deeds, meaning doing what God has commanded to be done and refraining from what God has forbidden, that they will have a good reward, meaning: a great reward for them from God for their belief in God and His Messenger, and their righteous deeds in this world, and that reward is Paradise which the righteous have been promised.

And His saying, remaining therein forever means eternal, they will not move from it, nor will they be transferred. The accusative of remaining is in the state of His saying, that they will have a good reward in this state in the state of their remaining in that reward. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: And give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward, abiding therein forever: meaning in an eternal home in which they will not die, those who believed in what you brought from God, and did what you commanded them.

x: God Almighty says: Muhammad also warns the people who said, ‘God has taken a son,’ from among the polytheists of his people and others, of God’s wrath, His immediate vengeance, and His delayed punishment, for what they said.

c: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: And warn those who say, ‘God has taken a son,’ meaning the Quraysh in their saying, We only worship the angels, who are the daughters of God. And His statement, They have no knowledge of it, is saying: What do those who say this statement, meaning their saying, God has taken a son, have by it: meaning by God, from knowledge, and the ha in His statement, by it is from the mention of God. Rather, the meaning of the statement is: What do those who say this statement about God, that it is not permissible for Him to have a son, have knowledge of? So they said that out of their ignorance of God and His greatness.

x: And his saying, nor for their fathers means: nor for their ancestors who passed before them on the same as they are today, they had knowledge of God and His greatness. And his saying, a great word that comes out of their mouths the reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Medina, Kufa and Basra read it as a great word with the accusative of the word meaning: their word that they said was a great word on the interpretation, as it is said: a good man Amr, and a good man a man stood, and a good man stood.

i: And some of the grammarians of Basra said:
x: the word was put in the accusative because it is in the meaning: a great word by it, as God Almighty said: And an evil resting place and he said it is in the accusative like the saying of the poet: I knew that if the vaccine was to be given to the king, he would throw it north.

That is, the winds blow them northward, so it is as if he said: That word is great. It was mentioned about some of the Meccans that he used to read it as Kabbar Kalima in the nominative case, as one says: Your saying is great and your status is great. If it is read in this way, then there is no implied word in his saying Kabbar Kalima and it is an attribute of the word. The correct reading in this, in my opinion, is the reading of those who read Kabbar Kalima in the accusative case, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it. So the interpretation of the statement is: The word is great, a word that comes out of the mouths of these people who said: God has taken a son, and the angels are the daughters of God.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: “A grave word that comes out of their mouths is their saying: The angels are daughters of God.” And His saying, They say nothing but a lie, the Almighty says: What these people who say that God has taken a son say with their saying is nothing but a lie, a slander they have fabricated against God.

x: He, the Most High, means by that: Perhaps, O Muhammad, you will kill yourself and destroy yourself in the footsteps of your people who said to you, We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or out of rebellion against their Lord, if they do not believe in this book that you sent down to you and believe that it is from God, out of grief, longing, and sorrow, by turning away from you, and turning away from what you brought them and abandoning belief in you. It is said from this: So-and-so humbled himself, he humbled himself, and from this is the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: Oh, you who are so consumed with grief for something that fate has carved out of your hands! He wants to carve it, so it became lighter. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying Bakhe’, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Perhaps you would kill yourself with death meaning: kill yourself.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: the same. As for his saying, regrettably, the people of interpretation differed in its interpretation.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: Perhaps you will kill yourself with anger if they do not believe in this hadith.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: If they do not believe in this hadith, out of grief. He said: Anger.

x: Others said: Anxiety.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God with grief, he said: with impatience.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. And others said: Its meaning is: out of grief for them.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, and he said:
m: Sorry, he said: Out of grief for them. We have already explained the meaning of regret in the past of this book, so there is no need to repeat it here. This is a reproach from God Almighty for his sorrow over his people’s distancing themselves from him in what he called them to of belief in God and disavowal of gods and rivals, and He was merciful to them. And in the same way as we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Perhaps you will kill yourself with grief over them, if they do not believe in this message. He was rebuking him for his grief over them when he missed out on what he had hoped for from them: that is, do not do it.

x: And His statement, Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, the Almighty says: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for the earth, that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed, meaning: That We may test Our servants as to which of them will abandon it and follow Our commands and prohibitions and act in it in obedience to Us. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, There is no adornment for it on the earth, he said: There is nothing on it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Indeed, We have made what is on the earth an adornment for it, he mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The world is green and sweet, and God has made you successors in it, so He will see how you act, so beware of the world, and beware of women. As for his saying,
h
We will test them as to which of them is best in deed
, the people of interpretation said in their interpretation something similar to what we said about it.

x: Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Asim Al-Asqalani told us, he said:
m: h
We will test them as to which of them is best in deed
. He said: Leave it to her.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Indeed, We have made what is on the earth adornment for it that We may test them as to which of them is best in deed. A test for them as to which of them will follow My command and act in obedience to Me. And His statement, And indeed, We will make that which is upon it a barren plain, the Almighty says: And indeed, We will destroy it after We have cultivated it with the adornments We have placed upon it, and We will turn it into a barren plain with no vegetation, crops, or plantings upon it. It has been said that what is meant by the plain in this place is: the flat surface of the earth, and that is similar in meaning to what we say in that regard. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, and in the sense of the jarz, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said:

c: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And We will make what is on it a barren plain
, meaning: Everything on it will perish and be destroyed.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, A barren plain, he said: A desolate place.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And indeed, We will make what is upon it a barren plain. And the plain is the land in which there are no trees or plants.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: h
And We will make what is on it a barren plain
. Meaning: The earth, and what is on it will perish and disappear, and the return will be to Me. So do not despair, and do not be saddened by what you hear and see in it.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, a barren plain, he said: A barren land is a land in which there is nothing. Don’t you see that He says, Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops? He said: And barren land is nothing in it, neither plants nor benefits. And the plain is the level. And he recited, You will not see therein any crookedness or unevenness. He said: Level. It is said: The land is barren, so it is barren, and the locusts and cattle barren it, and the lands are ajraaz if there is nothing in it. And the barren year is called barren and ajraaz years because of its barrenness, dryness and lack of rain. The rajaz poet said: The years have swept them away It is said: The people became barren if their land became barren, and they became barren of their land if they ate all of its plants.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Or do you think, O Muhammad, that the People of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our signs a wonder? Indeed, what I created of the heavens and the earth, and what is in them of wonders, is more amazing than the matter of the People of the Cave, and My proof for all of that is established against these polytheists from your people, and others from among My servants. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
m: ? Surat Al-Kahf.

c: The verse Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were

, among Our signs, a wonder? Muhammad ibn Amr said in his hadith, he said: They are not a wonder, the most amazing of Our signs. Al-Harith said in his hadith, with their saying: The most amazing of Our signs: They are not the most amazing of Our signs.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his statement,
h
Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were
, among Our signs, a wonder? They used to say, They are a wonder.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were
, among Our signs, a wonder? He said: There were among Our signs what was more wondrous than that.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq:
m: Or do you think that the People of the Cave and the Inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder? That is, what they had estimated in what I did regarding the affairs of creation, and what I placed upon the servants of My proofs, is greater than that.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Or do you think, O Muhammad, that the People of the Cave and the Inscription were among Our wondrous signs? Indeed, what I have given you of knowledge and wisdom is better than it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were

, among Our signs, a wonder? He said: What I have given you of knowledge, the Sunnah, and the Book is better than the affair of the companions of the cave and the inscription. Rather, we said: The first statement is more deserving of the interpretation of the verse, because God Almighty revealed the story of the People of the Cave to His Prophet as an argument against the polytheists of his people, as we mentioned in the narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, when they asked him about it as a test of his truthfulness in answering it. So, rebuking them for their denial of what was more pressing for them in the argument than what they asked about them, and they claimed that they would believe when they answered it, was more similar to the report of what God bestowed upon His Messenger of blessings. As for the cave, it is the mountain cave to which the people whose story God told in this surah took refuge. As for the inscription, the people of interpretation differed about its meaning.

x: Some of them said: It is the name of a village or a valley, although there is disagreement among them about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya bin Abdul A’la and Abdul Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Ka’b claims that Ar-Raqim is the village.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription
He said: Ar-Raqim is a valley between Ghasfan and Ayla, not far from Palestine, and it is close to Ayla.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said:
m: I heard my father, on the authority of Atiyah, he said: Ar-Raqim is a valley.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
Or do you think that the Companions of the Cave and the Inscription
? We were told that the Inscription was the valley in which the Companions of the Cave were.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb,
m: Surat al-Kahf 18:9
h
Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were
, among Our signs, a wonder? on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, the inscription, he said: Ka’b claims that it is the village.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, the inscription, he said: Some of them say: the inscription is their book of divisions, and some of them say: it is the valley in which their cave is.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: As for the cave, it is the cave of the valley, and Ar-Raqim is the name of the valley.

x: Others said: Ar-Raqim is the book.
Who said that?

c: Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription
means: the book.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: My father told us, on the authority of Ibn Qais, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: The inscription is a tablet of stones on which they wrote the stories of the People of the Cave, then they placed it at the door of the cave.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said:
m: Ar-Raqim is a book, and that book is a report, so God did not tell about that book and what is in it, and he recited: And what will make you know what is ‘Aliyyun? It is a book inscribed, witnessed by those brought near. “And what will make you know what is ‘Masjid’? It is a book inscribed.”

x: Others said: Rather, it is the name of the mountain of the Companions of the Cave.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: Ar-Raqim is the mountain in which the cave is.

x: It has been said that the name of that mountain is: Banjlus.

c: Ibn Hamid told us that.
m: He said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas. It has been said that his name was Banajlus.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Wahb bin Sulayman told me, on the authority of Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʿi,
m: that the name of the cave mountain is Banajlus. The name of the cave is Haizam, and the name of the dog is Khamran. It has been narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding Ar-Raqim what:

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: I know all of the Qur’an, except for Hanan, Al-Awah, and Ar-Raqim.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Amr ibn Dinar told me that
m: he heard Ikrimah say: Ibn Abbas said: I do not know what the inscription is, a book or a building. The first of these sayings that is correct about the inscription is that it means: a tablet, or a stone, or something on which a book was written. The historians said: It is a tablet on which were written the names of the People of the Cave and their story when they took refuge in the cave. Then some of them said: That tablet was taken to the king’s treasury. And some of them said: Rather, it was placed on the door of their cave. And some of them said: Rather, it was preserved with some of the people of their country. And the inscription is: Fa’il, its origin is: Marqum, then it was changed to Fa’il, just as the wounded is called: Jareeh, and the murdered is: Qatyl, it is said from it: I wrote such and such: if you wrote it, and from it the inscription on the garment is called a raqm, because it is the line by which its price is known. And from that the snake is called: Arqam, because of the traces on it, and the Arabs say: On you the raqmah, and leave the bank: meaning on you the raqmah of the valley where the water is, and leave the bank side. And the two banks: the two sides of the valley. And I think that the one who said the raqmah: the valley, went with it to this, I mean by it the raqmah of the valley.

x: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Or do you think that the companions of the cave and the inscription were, among Our signs, a wonder? When the young men, the companions of the cave, took refuge in the mountain cave, fleeing with their religion to God, they said when they took refuge there: Our Lord, grant us mercy from You, desiring from their Lord, that He would grant them mercy from Him. And His statement:
h
And prepare for us from our affair right guidance

means: And they said: Make easy for us what we seek and what we seek of Your pleasure and escape from disbelief in You, and from the worship of idols to which our people call us, right guidance: He says: Correctness in doing what You love. Scholars have differed about the reason for the fate of these young men in the cave, which God mentioned in His Book.

Some of them said: The reason for that was that they were Muslims who followed the religion of Jesus, and they had an idol-worshipping king who called them to worship idols, so they fled with their religion from him, fearing that he would tempt them away from their religion, or kill them, so they hid from him in the cave.
Those who said that mentioned: Ibn Humayd narrated: Al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated: Amr narrated regarding His statement,
h
The Companions of the Cave and the Inscription

, that the youths were of the religion of Jesus, Islam, and their king was an unbeliever. He had brought out an idol for them, but they refused and said, “Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon any god besides Him. We would have certainly said an outrageous thing then.” He said: So they separated from their people to worship God. One of them said: My father had a cave in which he sheltered his sheep, so let us go and stay in it. They entered it and were lost at that time, so they were searched for. It was said: They entered this cave. Their people said: We do not want for them a punishment or torment more severe than to fill up this cave over them. So they built it over them and then filled it up.
Then God sent a king over them who followed the religion of Jesus and raised that structure that had been filled up over them.

Some of them said to each other, How long have you stayed? They said, We stayed a day or part of a day. Until he reached, Then send one of you with this silver of yours to the city. And the silver at that time was large, so they sent one of them to bring them food. And a drink, and when he went to go out, he saw something at the door of the cave that he did not like, so he wanted to go back, then he continued until he entered the city, and he did not like what he saw, then he took out a dirham, and they looked at it and did not like it, and they did not like the dirham, and they said: Where did you get this from? This is made of paper from a time other than this. And they gathered around him asking him, and they did not stop until they went with him to their king, and their people had a tablet on which they wrote what would happen, so they looked at that tablet, and the king asked him, and he told him about his matter, and they looked in the book when it was lost, so they were happy with him and his companions, and it was said to him: Go with us and show us your companions, so he went and they went with him, so that he could show them, and he entered before the people, and he struck their ears, and those who were overcome by their matter said: We will build a mosque over them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said:
m: The affair of the people of the Gospel was confused, sins became great among them, and kings became arrogant among them, until they worshipped idols and sacrificed to tyrants. There were still among them those who followed the command of Jesus, son of Mary, adhering to the worship of God and His Oneness. Among those who did that was a king from the Romans called Decius. He had worshipped idols, sacrificed to tyrants, and killed whoever opposed him in that from among those who adhered to the religion of Jesus, son of Mary. He would settle in the villages of the Romans, and he would not leave in any village where he settled anyone who followed the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, except that he would kill him, until he worshipped idols and sacrificed to tyrants, until Decius settled in the city of the young men of the cave. When Decius settled there, that was too much for the people of faith, so they feared him and fled in every direction. And Decius had made it easy for them to follow the people of faith and gather for him, and he had taken a police from the infidels from its people, so they began to follow the people of faith in the places where they hid, and they brought them out to Decius, so he brought them to the gatherings in which the sacrifices were made for the tyrants, and he gave them the choice between saving death and worshipping idols and sacrificing for the tyrants, so some of them desired life and were horrified by death and were tempted, and some of them refused to worship other than God and were killed. When the steadfast people of faith in God saw that, they began to surrender themselves to torment and killing, so they were killed and cut up, then the pieces of their bodies were tied up and hung on the city wall from all sides, and on every gate of it, until the temptation became great for the people of faith, so some of them disbelieved and were abandoned, and some of them were crucified for their religion and were killed. When the young men of the cave saw that, they were deeply saddened, until their colors changed and their bodies became thin, and they sought help in prayer and fasting. And charity, praise, glorification, declaration of God’s greatness and magnification, weeping, and supplication to God. They were young, free men, sons of the Roman nobles.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: I was told that some of them had teeth as white as paper, because of their young age. Ibn Abbas said: They were like that in worshipping God day and night, crying to God and seeking His help. They were eight men: Maksalmina, who was the eldest of them, and he was the one who spoke to the king on their behalf, and Muhsimilinina, and Yamlikha, and Martus, and Kashutush, and Berunus, and Dinamus, and Yatunus Qalus. When Decius decided to gather the people of the village to worship idols and sacrifice to the tyrants, they cried to God and supplicated to Him, and they began to say: O God, Lord of the heavens and the earth, we will not call upon any god other than You. We would have said then an outrage. Remove this trial from Your believing servants and repel the calamity from them and bestow blessings upon Your servants who believed in You and prevented Your worship except in secret, concealing that, until they worship You openly! While they were in that state, their leaders among the infidels, who were gathering the people of the city to worship idols and sacrifice to the tyrants, recognized them and mentioned their affair. They had been alone in their prayer place, worshipping God there and supplicating to Him, and expecting to be mentioned to Decius. So those infidels set out until they entered their prayer place, and found them prostrating on their faces, supplicating, weeping, and asking God to save them from Decius and his temptation. When those infidel leaders among them saw them, they said to them: What kept you from the king’s command? They went to him, then left them, and reported their matter to Decius, and said: The people have gathered to sacrifice to your gods, and these are young men from your household, who mock you, and ridicule you, and disobey your command, and abandon your gods, and they set up a prayer place for them and the companions of Jesus, son of Mary, to pray in it, and to supplicate to their god and the god of Jesus and the companions of Jesus, so why have you left them to do this while they are in the midst of your sultan and kingdom? They are eight men, their leader is Maksalmina, and they are the sons of the city’s nobles. When they said that to Decius, he sent for them, and brought them from the prayer place where they were, their eyes overflowing with tears and their faces covered in dust. He said to them: What prevented you from witnessing the sacrifice to our gods that are worshipped on earth, and from making yourselves an example for the leaders of your city, and for those of us who are present from among the people? Choose from me: Either you sacrifice to our gods as the people sacrifice, or I will kill you. Then Maksalmina said: We have a god whom we worship, whose greatness fills the heavens and the earth. We will never call upon anyone other than Him, and we will never acknowledge this to which you call us. Rather, we worship God, our Lord, to Him be praise, glorification, and exaltation from our souls, purely forever. Him we worship, and from Him we ask for salvation and goodness. As for the tyrants and their worship, we will never acknowledge them, and we will not be slaves to the devils, nor will we make ourselves and our bodies slaves to them, after God has guided us to Him, out of fear of you or in awe of you. Your slavery, do with us as you please. Then the companions of Maksalmina said to Decius as he had said. He said: When they said that to him, he ordered them to be stripped of the garments that were on them from the garments of their leaders, then he said: As for you have done what you have done, I will delay you until you are among the people of my kingdom and my entourage and the people of my country and I will travel to you, so I will fulfill for you what I promised you of punishment. And nothing prevents me from hastening that for you except that I see you as young men, and I do not think that I will destroy you until I am satisfied with you, and I will make for you a term in which you will remember and review your minds. Then he ordered the ornaments that were on them of gold and silver to be stripped off, then he ordered them to leave him, and Decius went from his place to a city other than their city, which they were in, close to it, for some of what he wanted of his affair. When the young men saw that Decius had left their city, they hastened his arrival, and they were afraid that if he came to their city, they would be remembered. So they conspired among themselves that each one of them should take a provision from his father’s house, give it in charity, and take provisions with what was left, then go to a cave near the city in a mountain called Panjalus, and stay there and worship God until Decius returned. They would come to him and stand before him, and he would do with them as he wished. When some of them said that to each other, each young man took from his father’s house a provision, gave it in charity, and set out with what remained of their provision, followed by a dog of theirs, until they came to that cave in that mountain, and they remained in it, doing nothing but praying, fasting, glorifying, praising, and extolling God, seeking the face of God Almighty and the life that never ends. And they assigned their provision to a young man of theirs called Yamlikha, who was in charge of their food, buying their provisions from the city secretly from its people, because he was one of the most handsome and brave of them. Yamlikha used to do that, so when he entered the city, he would put on the clothes that were nice on him, and take clothes like the clothes of the poor who eat there, then he would take his paper, and go to the city and buy them food and drink, and listen and spy on them, to see if he and his companions were mentioned in anything among the people of the city, then he would return to his companions with their food and drink, and tell them what he had heard of the report of the people, and they remained like that for as long as they remained. Then the tyrant Decius went to the city from which he had come to his own city, which was the city of Ephesus, and he ordered the nobles of its people to slaughter for the tyrants. The people of faith were terrified by that, Surat al-Kahf 18:10 When the young men took refuge in the cave, they said, "Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself and facilitate for us from our affair right guidance." so they hid in every hiding place. Yamlikha was in the city buying food and drink for his companions with some of their expenses. He returned to his companions crying and with a little food, and he informed them that the tyrant Decius had entered the city, and that they had been remembered and missed and sought with the nobles of the city to slaughter for the tyrants.

c: When he told them
m: this, they were terribly frightened, and fell prostrate on their faces, calling upon God, beseeching Him, and seeking refuge in Him from the tribulation. Then Yamlikha said to them: O my brothers, raise your heads, and eat from this food that I have brought you, and trust in your Lord. So they raised their heads, and their eyes were overflowing with tears, wary and fearful for themselves, and they ate from it, and that was at sunset. Then they sat talking and studying, and reminding each other of the report, with sadness on their part, fearing what their companion had brought them. While they were in that state, God struck their ears in the cave for a number of years, and their dog stretched out his arms at the door of the cave, and what befell them befell them while they were believers, certain, believing in the promise, and their expenses were placed with them. When the next day came, Decius missed them, so he looked for them but did not find them, so he said to the leaders of the city: The situation of these young men who They went, for they thought that I was angry with them for what they had done at the beginning of their affair, because of their ignorance of what they had been ignorant of My affair. I would not be ignorant of them in Myself, and I will not hold any of them accountable for anything if they repent and worship My gods. If they had done so, I would have left them alone and not punished them for anything they had done in the past. Then the leaders of the city said to him: You are not worthy of having mercy on a people who are wicked, rebellious, and disobedient, persisting in their injustice and disobedience. I have granted them a term and delayed the punishment that I inflicted on others. If they had wanted, they could have returned at that term, but they did not repent, nor did they desist, nor did they regret what they had done. Since you set out, they have been squandering their wealth in the city. When they learned of your arrival, they fled and were not seen again. So if you wish to bring them, send to their fathers and test them, and be strict with them so that they may lead you to them, for they are hiding from you. When they said that to the mighty Decius, he became very angry. Then he sent for their fathers, and brought them. He asked them about them and said: Tell me about your rebellious sons who disobeyed my command and abandoned my gods. Bring them to me and inform me of their whereabouts. Their fathers said to him: As for us, we did not disobey your command and did not oppose you. We worshipped your gods and sacrificed to them. Why did you kill us among a rebellious people who took our money and squandered it and destroyed it in the markets of the city? Then they set out and climbed a mountain called Pangalus, between which and the city there is a distant land, fleeing from you? When they said that, he let them go, and began to wonder what to do with the young men. Then God Almighty suggested to him that he should order the cave to be closed off to them as an honor from God. He wanted to honor them and the bodies of the young men, so that nothing would wander or circle around them. He wanted to revive them and make them a sign for a nation that would succeed them, and to show them that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it, and that God will raise those in the graves. So Decius ordered the cave to be closed off to them, and he said: Leave these rebellious young men who have abandoned my gods, let them die as they are in the cave, thirsty and hungry, and let their cave which they chose for themselves be a place of disavowal for them. So Adhu did that to them, thinking that they were awake and knew what would happen to them, but God had taken their souls in a sleep, and their dog was stretching out his arms at the door of the cave, and God had covered him with what covered them, turning to the right and to the left. Then two believing men were in the house of King Decius, who concealed their faith: one of them was called Pedros, and the other was called Ronas. So they decided to write down the story of the young men of the cave, their genealogies, their names, and the names of their fathers, and the story of their life on two lead tablets. Then they would make a copper coffin for it, put the two tablets in it, and write on it at the mouth of the cave between the two buildings. They would seal the coffin with their seals, and they said: Perhaps God will cause these young men to appear as believers before the Day of Resurrection, so that whoever is opened to them will know their life when he reads this book. So they did, and they built a building over it, and Decius and the generation of them who were from them remained as long as God willed them to remain. Then Decius and the generation who were with him perished, and many generations after him, and successors came after successors. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Abdullah ibn Katheer narrated: Mujahid narrated: The People of the Cave were the sons of the nobles of their city, and the people of honor. They went out and gathered behind the city without an appointment. A man among them, who was the oldest, said: I find something in myself that I do not think anyone else finds. They said: What do you find? He said: I find in myself that my Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. They said: We find it. So they all stood up and said: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never invoke besides Him any god. We would have certainly said an outrageous thing then. So they gathered to enter the cave, and over their city at that time was a tyrant called Daqinus. They remained in the cave for three hundred years and nine more. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Dawud, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubayd bin Umair, who said: The People of the Cave were young kings, with their forelocks covered in armor, and they had their hunting dog with them. They went out on a great festival of theirs in a costume and procession, and they brought out with them their gods that they worshipped. God cast faith into the hearts of the young men, so they believed. Each one of them hid his faith from his companion, so they said to themselves, without revealing their faith to one another: We will leave these people so that no punishment will befall us for their crime. A young man from among them went out until he reached the shade of a tree, and sat in it. Then another came out and saw him sitting alone, hoping that he would be in the same situation without revealing it, so he came and sat next to him. Then the others went out, so they came and sat next to them, and they gathered together.

x: Some of them said: What brought you together?

Another said: Rather, what brought you together? And each concealed his faith from his companion for fear of himself. Then they said: Let two young men from among you come out and be alone, and they pledge not to disclose anything to the other, then each one of them discloses his affair to the other, for we hope that we will be on one issue. So two young men from among them came out and they pledged themselves, then they spoke, and each one of them mentioned his affair to the other, so they came with good tidings to their companions, having agreed on one issue, and behold, they were all on the faith, then there was a cave in the mountain near them, and some of them said to the other: Come to the cave, Your Lord will spread for you from His mercy and will prepare for you from your affair ease. So they entered the cave with their hunting dog and slept, and God made it one sleep for them, so they slept for three hundred years and nine more.

He said: And their people lost them, so they sought them and sent hail, and God blinded them to their traces and their cave, so when they could not find them, they wrote their names and lineages on a tablet: So-and-so, son of so-and-so, and so-and-so, son of So-and-so, the sons of our kings, we lost them on such-and-such a holiday, in such-and-such a month, in such-and-such a year, in the kingdom of so-and-so, son of so-and-so. They removed the tablet to the treasury, and that king died and a Muslim king prevailed over them along with the Muslims. Century after century came, and they remained in their cave for three hundred years, and they increased by nine.
Others said: Rather, their fate was to go to the cave to escape the pursuit of a sultan who sought them because of a claim of a crime that he claimed against a friend of theirs.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us: Ismail bin Sharous told me that
m: he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: The disciple of Jesus, son of Mary, came to the city of the People of the Cave and wanted to enter it. He was told: There is an idol at its gate, and no one enters it without prostrating to it. He was reluctant to enter it, so he went to a bathhouse, which was near that city, and he worked there, renting himself out to the owner of the bathhouse. The owner of the bathhouse saw the blessing in his bathhouse and the abundance of his livelihood, so he began to offer him Islam and began to talk to him. Young men from the city hung up on him, and he began to tell them report of the heavens and the earth and the afterlife, until they believed in him and believed him. They were like him in his good appearance. He used to stipulate to the owner of the bathhouse that the night would be mine and not come between me and the prayer when it was due. He remained like that until the son of the king brought a woman and entered the bathhouse with her. The disciple taunted him and said: You are the son of the king, and you enter this miserable woman with you? He felt ashamed, so he went and came back again, and he said the same thing to him, so he cursed him and rebuked him and did not turn back until he entered and the woman entered with him, and they both died in the bath. The king was brought and it was said to him: The owner of the bath killed your son, so he searched, but he could not find him, so he fled. He said: Who was his companion? So they named the young men, and they named them, and they left the city, and they passed by a friend of theirs in his farm, and he was in the same situation as them, and they mentioned that they searched, and the dog went with them, until night came upon them at the cave, so they entered it, and they said: We will spend the night here, then in the morning, if God wills, we will see what you think. So he beat their ears, and the king went out with his companions, following them until they found them entering the cave, and whenever a man wanted to enter, he was terrified, so no one could enter it, so someone said: If you had control over them, would you not have killed them? He said: Yes. He said: Then build a door to the cave over them, and leave them in it to die of thirst and hunger, so he did.

evidence.text: They would seal the coffin with their seals, and they said: Perhaps God will cause these young men to appear as believers before the Day of Resurrection, so that whoever is opened to them will know their life when he reads this book.

x: God, the Most High, means by His statement,
h
So We struck their ears in al-Kahf 18
h
So We struck

their ears with sleep in the cave? That is, We cast sleep upon them, as one says to another: May God strike you with paralysis, meaning that God afflicted him with it and sent it upon him. And His statement, a number of years means a numbered number of years, and the number is accusative in His statement,
h
So We struck
. And His statement,
h
Then We raised them up that We might know which of the two parties had counted best

means: Then We raised up these youths who had taken refuge in God after We had struck their ears in it for a number of years of their sleep, so that My servants might see and know by research, which of the two groups of God differed in the amount of time that the youths had stayed in their cave sleeping. He counted how long they had stayed means: It is more correct to estimate how long they had stayed in it, and by time he means: the limit, as An-Nabigha said: Except for someone like you or someone you are ahead of, the horse will outrun when it seizes the lead.
He mentioned that those who differed in this matter were some of the youths.
Some of them said: Both parties were infidels.
Some of them said: Rather, one of them was a Muslim and the other was an infidel.
Mention of who said: The two parties were from the young people.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: meaning the two parties from the people of the young men.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Then We raised them up that We might test which of the two parties had best calculated the time that they had tarried
, meaning: Neither of the two groups had knowledge, neither their disbelievers nor their believers. As for his statement, a period, the people of interpretation differed about its meaning.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is: far away.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, When they remained for a period of time, meaning: a long time.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: a number.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Amda he said:
m: a number.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. And in the accusative case of his statement a period, there are two views: One of them? That it is accusative as an explanation of his statement counted, as if it was said: Which of the two parties is more correct in number for the amount of their stay? And this is the more correct of the two views in that, because the explanation of the people of interpretation came with that. The other: that it is in the accusative case because his saying they stayed occurred to it, as if he said: Which of the two parties has the greatest time for staying?

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We, O Muhammad, relate to you the report of these young men who sought refuge with God, in truth, meaning: with honesty and certainty that is without doubt. They are young men who believed in their Lord. He says: The young men who sought refuge with God, about whom the leaders of the polytheists of your people asked you about their report, are young men who believed in their Lord. And We increased them in guidance. He says: And We increased their faith in their Lord, faith, and insight into their religion, until they were patient in abandoning the home of their people, and fleeing from among them with their religion to God, and leaving what they were in of a lowly and easy life, to the roughness of staying in the mountain cave.
And His saying,
h
And We strengthened their hearts
, the Almighty says: And We inspired them with patience, and strengthened their hearts with the light of faith until their souls turned away from the lowly life they were living.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And We strengthened their hearts
, he says: with faith. And His statement,
h
When they stood up and said

, ‘Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth,’ he says: when they stood up before the tyrant Decius, they said to him when he rebuked them for abandoning the worship of his gods: Our Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, he says: they said, “Our Lord is the King of the heavens and the earth and everything in them, and your gods are subservient, and it is not permissible for us to abandon the worship of the Lord and worship the subservient. We will not call upon any god other than Him,” he says: we will not call upon any god other than the Lord of the heavens and the earth, because there is no god other than Him, and everything other than Him is His creation. Indeed, then, we have spoken an outrageous thing, He, the Most High, says: If we call upon any god other than the God of the heavens and the earth, then we have spoken an outrageous thing in our calling upon any god other than Him, meaning an extreme lie, exceeding its limit in falsehood and exaggeration, as the poet said: Oh my people, my critics have gone too far and claim that my falsehood has destroyed my right. It is said: So-and-so went too far in the price if he exceeded the limit and rose, he goes too far and too high. As for distance, it is said: So-and-so’s house went too far, he goes too far, and from length: the girl went too far, she goes too far and too high: if she became tall. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying excessive the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
We would have said an outrage
, meaning a lie.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
We would have said something outrageous
, he said: We would have said something wrong, he said: Excess is a mistake in speech.

x: The Almighty says, informing about what the young men from the companions of God said: These are our people who have taken for themselves other gods besides God, whom they worship besides Him.
h
Why do they not bring for them a clear proof

? He says: Why do they not bring for their worship of them a clear argument? In the word la there is an omission, and what is apparent is sufficient for what was omitted, and that is in His statement:
h
Why do they not bring for them a clear proof

? The ha and the mim in for them are from the mention of the gods, and the gods are not brought for them a proof, and the authority is not asked for them, but rather their worshippers are asked for the authority to worship them. So it is known, since the matter is thus, that the meaning of the speech is: Why do they not bring for their worship of them, and their taking of them as gods besides God a clear proof. And similar to what we said about the meaning of the authority, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, Why do they not produce against them a clear authority? He said: A clear excuse. And what he meant by the statement of God Almighty, Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God? And who is more deviant in his transgression in associating partners with God than he who invents and fabricates a lie against God, and associates with God in His authority a partner whom he worships instead of Him, and takes him as a god.

x: God Almighty says, informing about what some young men said to others: And when you withdraw, O young men, from your people who have taken for themselves gods besides God, “and they worship none but God. He says: And when you withdraw from your people who worship other than God, then what is its meaning is in the accusative case, in apposition to the ha’ and the mim in His statement, And when you withdraw from them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And when you withdrew from them and what they worship except God, and it is in the Mushaf of Abdullah, and what they worship other than God, this is its interpretation. As for his saying,
h
So take refuge in the cave

, what he means by that is: So go to the cave of the mountain called Banglos, your Lord will spread out for you from His mercy, meaning: Your Lord will spread out for you from His mercy by making it easy for you to get out of the matter that you were thrown into by Kafr Daqinus and by His request for you to expose you to temptation. His saying,
h
So take refuge in the cave

, is an answer to when, the meaning of the statement was: And when you, O people, have isolated yourself from your people, then take refuge in the cave, as it is said: If you sin, then seek forgiveness from God and repent to Him. His saying, And He will prepare for you a way out of your matter, means: And He will make easy for you from the matter that you are in of grief and distress, fearing for yourselves and your religion, a way out. What he means by the way out is: something that you find comfort in. And there are two languages for the way out of the hand and other than the hand: a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa, and a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the fa. Al-Kisa’i used to deny the human elbow which is in the hand except by opening the fa’ and breaking the mim, and Al-Farra’ used to narrate them both, I mean the elbow of the matter and the two soft hands, and he used to recite in that the saying of the poet: I am more flexible than my elbow He says: Breaking the mim in it is better.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say in his saying from your affair something that you can use for comfort like a section, and comfort he made it a noun like a mosque, and it is a language they say rafq yarfiq murfaqan, and if you wish marfaq you mean raff and it was not read. The reciters differed in reading that, so most of the reciters of Medina read it wa yah'iha' lakum min amrkum with a fatha on the meem and a kasra on the fa, and most of the reciters of Iraq in the two cities read it marfaqan with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa. The correct thing to say about that is to say: they are two readings with one meaning, and reciters of the people of the Qur'an have read each of them, so the reciter reads with both of them and he is correct, but even if the matter is like that, then the one who chose in reading that wa yah'iha' lakum min amrkum with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa, because that is the more eloquent of the two languages and the most famous of them among the Arabs, and likewise in everything that is used for comfort.

The correct thing to say about that is to say: they are two readings with one meaning, and reciters of the people of the Qur'an have read each of them, so the reciter reads with both of them and he is correct, but even if the matter is like that, then the one who chose in reading that wa yah'iha' lakum min amrkum with a kasra on the meem and a fatha on the fa, because that is the more eloquent of the two languages and the most famous of them among the Arabs, and likewise in everything that is used for comfort.

x: God Almighty says,
h
And you will see the sun

, O Muhammad, when it rises, deviating from their cave on the right. What he means by his saying deviating is: straightening and leaning, from zur which means crookedness and inclination. It is said from it: in this land there is a zuur, if there is crookedness in it, and in so-and-so there is a zurar from so-and-so, if there is aversion in him from him. From this is the saying of Bishr ibn Abi Khazim: The camels flock to it, and there are palm trees in it, and there are two Abanin Azwar. It means symptoms and rust. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca and Basra read it as tazāwur with a shaddah on the zay, meaning: tatāzawur with two ta’s, then one of the ta’s was assimilated into the zay, as it was said: taḥāhirūna ‘alayhim. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as tazāwur with a light ta’ and zay, as if he meant tafa’al from az-zūr.

It was narrated from some of them as tazāwur with a light ta’ and a silent zay and a shaddah on the ra’ like tahmar, and some of them as tazāwwar like tahmar. The correct reading of this according to us is to say: They are two readings, I mean tazāwir with a light zay, and tazāwir with a heavy zay, well-known, and the reading of each of them is widespread among the readers of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so if the reader reads with them, he is correct. As for the other two readings, they are readings that I do not see as permissible to read, because they have an understandable aspect in Arabic, due to their deviation from the reading of the regions. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of his saying,
h
They turned away from their cave
, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Muhammad bin Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: h
And you will see the sun
, when it rises, inclining away from their cave on the right. He said: It inclines.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: She turned away from their cave on the right, meaning: She turned away from them.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And you will see the sun
when it rises, inclining away from their cave on the right,
h
and when it sets
, passing them by on the left, meaning: It inclines away from their cave to the right and to the left.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And you will see the sun
, when it rises, inclining away from their cave on the right, meaning: it inclines to the right, leaving them on the right.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
They turned away from their cave on the right
, he said:
h
They turned away from their cave on the right

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yazid bin Harun, on the authority of Sufyan bin Husayn, on the authority of Yaʿla bin Muslim, on the authority of Saʿid bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: If the sun were to rise on them, it would burn them, and if they did not turn over, the earth would consume them. He said: That is what He said:
h
And you will see the sun
, when it rises, inclining away from their cave on the right,
h
and when it sets
, passing them by on the left.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, he said: Musa bin Ismail told us, he said: Muhammad bin Muslim bin Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said:
m: It turns away from their cave means it inclines. And His statement,
h
And when it sets

, it approaches them on the left. God the Almighty says: And when the sun sets, it leaves them from their left. The meaning of the statement is: And you see the sun when it rises, turning away from their cave, and rising upon it from the right, so that it does not strike the young men, because if it rose upon them facing them, it would burn them and their clothes, or make them pale.
h
And when it sets

, it leaves them from the left, so that it does not strike them. It is said from this: I cut off such-and-such place: if I cut it off and passed it. And this is what some of the scholars of the speech of the Arabs from Basra used to say. As for the Kufians, they claim that it is alignment, and they mentioned that they heard from the Arabs: I cut it ahead and behind, and I followed it to the right and the left, and ahead and behind: meaning I was opposite it. They said: The qard and the qard have the same meaning. The origin of the qard is to cut, and it is said from it: I qardt the garment: if you cut it, and from it the scissors are called: scissors, because they cut, and from it the mouse cut the garment, and from it the saying of Dhu al-Rummah: To the women who lend their horses their saddles to the north, and to their right are the knights. He means by his saying: they lend: they cut off. And in the same way as we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And when it sets
, it leaves them on the left, meaning: it leaves them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, they said:
m: h
And when it sets
, it approaches them from the left.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, You leave them, he said: You leave them.

c: Al-Qasim told us: Al-Hussein told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And when it sets
, it leaves them to the left. He said: It leaves them to the left.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
It will leave them to the left
. He said:
h
It will leave them to the left

c: Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told us: Musa ibn Ismail told us: Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr:
m: h
And when it sets
, it leaves them. He said: It leaves them. And his statement:
h
And they are in a wide space thereof

. He said: And the young men who took refuge with him in a wide space thereof? It is plural: wide space, and Fajaa is extended. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And they are in a hollow of it. He said: In an open area of the cave. God said:
h
That is from the signs of God

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr,
m: And they are in a gap of it. He said: The inner place.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And they are in a gap of it, he said: the lost place.

c: Ibn Sinan told me, he said: Musa bin Ismail told us, he said: Muhammad bin Muslim Abu Saeed bin Abi Al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: In a gap of it, he said: In an internal place. And His saying,
h
That is from the signs of God

, the Almighty says: We did what We did to these young men whose story We told you about, by making them, when We wanted to strike their ears so that the sun would turn away from their beds to the right when it rose, and pass them by to the left when it set, while they were in a spacious place, so that the sun would not burn them and make them pale, nor would their clothes wear out due to their long sleep, so that they would rot on their bodies. This is from the proofs and evidence of God upon His creation, and the evidence by which those with understanding prove the greatness of His power and authority, and that nothing He wills is beyond His power. And His saying,
h
Whomsoever God guides

, he is the one who is guided, the Almighty says: Whoever God guides to be guided by His signs and evidence to the truth which He made evidence for Him, he is the one who is guided. He says: He is the one who has found the path of truth. And whoever God misguides He says: And whoever God misguides from His signs and evidence, and does not grant him success in using them to prove the right path. You will never find for him a guardian or ally to guide him He says: You will never find for him, O Muhammad, a friend or ally who will guide him to find it, because success and failure are in the hand of God. He grants success to whomever He wills of His servants, and fails whomever He wills. He says: So do not be saddened by the turning away of those of your people who have turned away from you and their denial of you, for if I had willed, I could have guided them and they would have believed, and in My hand is guidance and misguidance.

The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca and Basra read it as tazāwur with a shaddah on the zay, meaning: tatāzawur with two ta’s, then one of the ta’s was assimilated into the zay, as it was said: taḥāhirūna ‘alayhim.
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as tazāwur with a light ta’ and zay, as if he meant tafa’al from az-zūr.

The correct reading of this according to us is to say: They are two readings, I mean tazāwir with a light zay, and tazāwir with a heavy zay, well-known, and the reading of each of them is widespread among the readers of the regions, and they are close in meaning, so if the reader reads with them, he is correct.

As for the other two readings, they are readings that I do not see as permissible to read, because they have an understandable aspect in Arabic, due to their deviation from the reading of the regions.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And you, Muhammad, would think that these youths whose story We have told you, if you had seen them while We struck their ears in their cave to which they had taken refuge, were awake. And awake is the plural of awake, and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet: They found their brothers awake, and Saif was furious with them. And His statement,
h
And while they are asleep
, means: while they are asleep. And sleeping is the plural of sleeping, like sitting is the plural of sitting, and sitting is the plural of sitting. And His statement,
h
And We will turn them to the right and to the left
, means, the Most High, His praise is saying: And We will turn these youths in their sleep, sometimes to the right side, and sometimes to the left side.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And We turn them to the right and to the left
, and this turning is in their first sleep. He said: And it was mentioned to us that Abu Ayyad said: They have two turns every year.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Yazid,
m: who said: Sufyan ibn Husayn informed us, on the authority of Yaʿla ibn Muslim, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We shall turn them to the right and to the left, he said: If they did not turn them, the earth would eat them. And His statement,
h
And their dog stretching out his forelegs at the entrance
, the people of interpretation differed as to what God meant by His statement,
h
And their dog stretching out his forelegs
, some of them said: It was one of their dogs that was with them. We have already mentioned many of those who said that previously.
