x: Some of them said: It was a human being from among the people who cooked for them and followed them. As for the entrance, the people of interpretation differed as to its interpretation.
Some of them said: It is annihilation.
Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying in the courtyard means: in the courtyard.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Muhammad bin Abi al-Waddah told us, on the authority of Salim al-Aftas, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And their dog stretched out his forelegs at the entrance
. He said: At the courtyard.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, In the courtyard, he said: In the courtyard.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: By the entrance he said:
m: By the courtyard. Ibn Jurayj said: He holds the door of the cave.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And their dog was stretching out his forelegs at the entrance. He said: at the entrance to the cave.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement at the entrance he said:
m: at the courtyard of the cave.
b.via: his statement at the entrance he

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, By the threshold, that he meant by the courtyard.

x: Others said: The threshold is the plain.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And their dog stretching out his forelegs at the entrance
, meaning their courtyard, and it is said: the entrance is the plain.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Antarah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And their dog stretching out his forelegs
at the threshold, he said: The threshold is the plain.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Amr,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And their dog stretched out his forelegs at the entrance
, he said: The entrance is the ground, the dirt.

x: Others said: The entrance is the door.
Mention of those who said that: Surat al-Kahf 18:18 And you think them awake, while they are asleep.
h
And We turn them to the right and to the left
, while their dog is stretching out his two forelegs at the entrance.
h
If you had looked at them
, you would have turned from them in flight, and you would have been filled with terror of them.

c: Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Shabib, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And their dog stretched out his forelegs at the entrance

. He said: At the door. They said: At the courtyard. The most correct of the sayings is the saying of those who said: Al-Waseed is the door, or the courtyard of the door where the door is closed. This is because the door is closed, not closed: its closing due to its closure from the saying of God the Almighty: Indeed, it is closed upon them. There are two languages for it: Al-Aseed, which is the language of the people of Najd, and Al-Waseed: which is the language of the people of Tihamah. It was mentioned on the authority of Abu Amr bin Al-Ala’ that it is the language of Ahk Al-Yaman, and this is similar to their saying: Warakht Al-Kitab and Arakhtuhu, and Waaqaddad Al-Amr and Waaqaddad Al-Amr. Whoever said Al-Waseed said: I closed the door, so I closed it, and it is closed. Whoever said Al-Aseed said: I closed the door, so it is closed. So the meaning of the statement is:
h
And their dog stretched out his forelegs at the entrance
of their cave at the door, guarding their door for them. And His statement,
h
If you had looked at them
, you would have turned away from them in flight, means:
h
If you had looked at them

in their sleep in their cave, you would have turned away from them, fleeing from them. And you would have been filled with terror from them, means: And you would have filled your soul with fear from your looking at them, because God has clothed them with awe, so that no one can reach them, and no hand can touch them until the Book has fulfilled its term regarding them, and His power and authority awaken them from their sleep at the time He wanted to make them a lesson for whomever He wills of His creation, and a sign for whomever He wants to use them as an argument against Him from among His servants, so that they may know that the promise of God is true, and that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement,
h
And I would have been filled with terror from them
. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it with a shaddah on the lam in His statement,
h
And I would have been filled

, meaning that he would be filled time after time. The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it with a shaddah on the lam, meaning: I would have been filled once. And in our view, these are two widely-used readings, close in meaning, so whichever one the reciter reads, he is correct.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, And I would have been filled with terror from them.
The majority of the reciters of Medina read it with a shaddah on the lam in His statement, And I would have been filled, meaning that he would be filled time after time.
The majority of the reciters of Iraq read it with a shaddah on the lam, meaning: I would have been filled once.

x: God Almighty says: Just as We put these young men to sleep in the cave, and preserved them from being reached by anyone, and from the eye of a watcher looking at them, and preserved their bodies from affliction throughout time, and their clothes from rotting throughout the days by Our power, so We raised them from their sleep, and awakened them from their sleep, so that We might make them know the greatness of Our power, and the wonder of Our action in Our creation, and so that they might increase in their insight into their situation which they are upon, of their innocence from the worship of deities, and their sincerity to the worship of God alone, with no partner for Him, if they realize the length of time upon them, and they are in their state when they slept. And His statement, that they may ask one another, means that they may ask one another. One of them said, ‘How long did you stay?’

God Almighty says, So they asked one another, and one of them said to his companions, ‘How long did you stay?’ This is because they were surprised by their own long sleep. They said, ‘We stayed a day or part of a day.’ He says, “So the others answered him and said, ‘We stayed a day or part of a day,’ thinking that this was the case. Then the others said, ‘Your Lord knows best how long you stayed.’” So they surrendered the knowledge to God. And his saying,
h
Then send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city

, meaning their city from which they fled, which is called Ephesus. Then let him see which of them has the best food and bring you provision from it. He mentioned that they awoke from their sleep hungry, and that is why they asked for food.
He mentioned who said that, and he mentioned the reason for which he mentioned that they were raised from their sleep when they were raised from it:

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: Abdul-Razzaq narrated to us, he said: Muammar narrated to us, he said: Ismail bin Bishrus narrated to me, that
m: he heard Wahb bin Munabbih say: They became dust, meaning the young men of the People of the Cave, after the door of the cave was built over them for a period of time after a period of time. Then a shepherd was caught by rain at the cave, so he said: If only I would open this cave and bring my sheep in from the rain. He kept treating it until he opened what he had put in it, and returned their souls to their bodies the next day when they woke up. So they sent one of them with paper money to buy food. When he came to the door of their city, he saw something that he did not like, until he entered upon a man and said: Sell me food for these dirhams. He said: Where did you get these dirhams from? He said: I went out with some friends yesterday, and the night came upon us, then they came in the morning and sent me away. He said: These dirhams were during the reign of so-and-so, so where did you get them from? So he took it to the king, and he was a righteous king, and he said: Where did you get these dirhams from? He said: I went out with some friends last night, until night fell upon us in such and such a cave. Then they ordered me to buy them food. He said: Where are your friends? He said: In the cave. He said: So they set out with him until they came to the door of the cave. He said: Let me enter upon my friends before you. When they saw him and he approached them, he struck his ear and their ears, and every time a man entered, he terrified them, so they were not able to enter upon them. So they built a church near them and made it a mosque in which they prayed.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: The People of the Cave were the sons of the kings of the Romans. God granted them Islam, so they sought refuge in their religion and isolated themselves from their people until they reached the cave. God struck their hearing, so they remained for a long time until their nation perished and a Muslim nation came, and their king was a Muslim. They differed about the soul and the body. One said: He will resurrect the soul and the body together.

x: Another said: He will resurrect the soul, but the earth will eat the body and it will be nothing. Their king was upset by their differences, so he went and put on sackcloth and sat on the ashes. Then he called upon God, the Most High, and said: O Lord, you see the differences of these people, so send them a sign that will make it clear to them. So God sent the People of the Cave, and they sent one of them to buy food for them. He entered the market and began to recognize the faces, recognize the roads, and see faith in the city apparent. He went, and he was not afraid until he came to a man to buy food from him. When he looked... The man turned to the paper and denied it. He said: I think he said: They were like the hooves of a quarter, Surat al-Kahf 18:19 And thus We raised them up that they might ask one another. One of them said, "How long have you remained?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day."

They said, "Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city and let him see which of them has the best food, and let him bring you provision." From him,
h
and let him be gentle

and not let anyone know about you. meaning young camels. The young man said to him: Isn’t your king so-and-so? He said: Rather, our king is so-and-so. This continued between them until he brought it up to the king, who asked him.

c: The young man told him
m: the report of his companions. The king sent to the people and gathered them together. He said: You have differed in spirit and body, and God has sent you a sign. This is a man from the people of so-and-so, meaning their king who had passed away. The young man said: Take me to my companions. The king rode, and the people rode with him until they reached the cave. The young man said: Let me enter to my companions. When he saw them, he struck his ear and their ears. When they found him slow, the king entered, and the people entered with him. They saw bodies that they did not deny anything about, except that they had no souls. The king said: This is a sign that God has sent to you. Qatada said: On the authority of Ibn Abbas, he had gone on a military expedition with Habib bin Maslama, and they passed by the cave, and there were bones in it. A man said: These are the bones of the People of the Cave. Ibn Abbas said: Their bones were lost more than three hundred years ago.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: in what was mentioned in the hadith of the People of the Cave, he said: Then the people of that country were ruled by a righteous man called Theodosius. When he ruled, his rule lasted for sixty-eight years, and the people formed parties during his reign, and they were parties.

x: Some of them believed in God and knew that the Hour was true, and some of them lied. This was a great burden on the righteous king Theodosius, and he cried to God and supplicated to Him, and he was deeply saddened when he saw the people of falsehood increasing and prevailing over the people of truth and saying: There is no life but the life of this world, and only the souls will be resurrected, and not the bodies, and they forgot what was in the Book. So Theodosius began to send to those whom he thought were good, and that they were leaders in the truth, and they began to lie about the Hour, until they almost turned the people away from the truth and the religion of the disciples. When the righteous king Theodosius saw this, he entered his house and locked it behind him, and put on a sackcloth and put ashes under it, then sat on it, and he continued to do that night and day for a period.

He supplicates to God and cries to Him for what he sees in people. Then the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful, who hates the destruction of servants, wanted to show the youths of the cave, and show people their situation, and make them a sign for them and an argument against them, so that they may know that the Hour is coming without a doubt, and that He responds to His righteous servant Theodosius, and completes His favor upon him, so that He does not take away from him his kingdom, nor the faith that He gave him, and that he worships God and does not associate anything with Him, and that He gathers those who were scattered from the believers. So God cast into the soul of a man from the people of that country in which the cave was, and the mountain in which the cave was for that man was Panglaos, and that man’s name was Ulyas, that he should demolish the structure that was at the mouth of the cave, and build a pen for his sheep in it.

So he hired two workers, and they began to remove those stones and build that pen with them, until they removed what was at the mouth of the cave, until they opened the door of the cave from them, and God concealed them from the people with terror, so they claim that the bravest of those who want to see them as much as he can enter through the door of the cave, then advance until he sees their dog before them to the door of the cave. Asleep, when they removed the stones and opened the door of the cave, God, the Possessor of Power, Majesty and Authority, the Resurrector of the dead, permitted the youths to sit in the back of the cave. They sat, happy, their faces radiant and their souls content. They greeted one another, as if they had awakened at the hour they used to wake up at when they woke up at the same time they used to spend the night. Then they got up to pray and prayed, as they used to do.

They did not see, nor was anything seen in their faces, nor their skins, nor their colours that they would find strange, like their appearance when they slept the evening before, and they saw that their king, the tyrant Decius, was seeking them out and searching for them. When they finished their prayer as they used to do, they said to Limlikha, who was their financial provider, who used to buy their food and drink from the city, and he had brought them the report that Decius was seeking them out and asking about them: Tell us, my brother, what did the people say about us the evening before this tyrant? They thought that they had slept as they had some of the nights they had been sleeping, and it seemed to them that they had slept as long as they had ever slept on the night they had just woken up, until they asked each other, and some of them said to each other, How long have you been asleep?

They said, We have stayed a day or part of a day. They said, Your Lord knows best how long you have stayed. All that was easy for them. Then Yamlikha said to them, You have been missed and sought in the city, and he wants you to be brought today, so that you may be slaughtered for the tyrants, or he may kill you, and whatever God wills after that. Then Maksalmina said to them, “O my brothers, know that you will meet, so do not disbelieve after your belief when the enemy of God calls you, and do not deny the life that does not perish after your belief in God, and the life after death.” Then they said to Yamlikha, “Go to the city and hear what is said to us there today, and what we will be mentioned with before Decius, and be gentle, and do not let anyone notice us, and buy us food and bring it to us, for it has become yours, and give us more than the food you brought us, for it was little, for we have become hungry.”

So Yamlikha did as he used to do, and put off his clothes, and took the clothes he was disguised in, and took a note from their expenses that were with them, which were struck by the obedience of Decius the king, and he left. Yamlikha went out, and when he passed by the door of the cave, he saw the stones removed from the door of the cave, and he was amazed by them, then he passed by and did not care about them, until he came to the city, hiding, turning away from the road for fear that one of its people would see him, recognize him, and take him to Decius. The righteous servant did not realize that Decius and the people of his time had perished before that by three hundred and nine years, or whatever God willed of that, since between the time they slept and the time they woke up, there were three hundred and nine years. When Yamlikha saw the door of the city, he raised his eyes, and saw above the back of the door a sign that would be for the people of faith, if he was visible in it.

When he saw it, he was amazed and began to look at it secretly, so he looked right and left, and was amazed to himself, then he left that door, and turned to another door of its doors, and he looked and saw from that what surrounded the entire city, and he saw on every door something like that, so he began to imagine to him that the city was not the city that he knew, and he saw many people who had been innovated whom he had not seen before that. Then he walked and wondered and imagined that he was confused. Then he returned to the door from which he had come, and wondered to himself and said: I wonder, but this was yesterday evening. The Muslims used to hide this sign and make light of it, but today it is apparent to Ali, who is dreaming! Then he saw that he was not asleep, so he took his cloak and put it on his head, then he entered the city and walked in its market place, and he heard many people swearing by the name of Jesus, son of Mary.

This made him even more afraid, and he saw that he was confused. So he stood leaning his back against a wall of the city and said to himself: By God, I do not know what this is! As for yesterday evening, there is not a person on earth who mentions Jesus, son of Mary, except that he will be killed. As for tomorrow, I hear them, and every person who mentions the matter of Jesus is not afraid. Then he said to himself: Perhaps this is not the city that I know. I hear the speech of its people, but I do not know any of them. By God, I do not know of a city near our city. So he stood up confused, not turning in any direction. Then he met a young man from the people of the city, and he said to him: What is the name of this city, young man? He said: Its name is Afsus. He said to himself: Perhaps I am possessed, or something has taken my mind away. By God, it is right for me to hasten to leave it before I am disgraced there or some evil befalls me and I perish?

This is what Yamlikha told his companions when it became clear to them what was wrong with him. Then he came to and said: By God, if I had hastened to leave the city before he was aware of me, it would have been more intelligent for me. So he approached those who sold food, took out the papers he had with him, and gave them to one of them. He said: Sell me food with these papers, O servant of God. The man took them, looked at the printing and engraving of the paper, and was amazed by them. Then he threw them to one of his companions, who looked at them. Then they began to throw them among themselves, from man to man, and marvel at them. Then they began to consult among themselves, and some of them said to one another: This man has found a treasure that has been hidden in the ground for a long time. When he saw them consulting about him, he was very afraid, and began to tremble, thinking that they had become aware of him and recognized him, and that they only wanted to take him to their king Decius and hand him over to him.

Other people came to him but did not recognize him, so he said to them, very afraid of them: Wake up, get over it! You have taken my money and held back, and as for your food, I have no need of it. They said to him: "Who are you, O Faqih, and what is your business? By God, you have found one of the treasures of the ancients, and you want to hide it from us. Come with us, and we will show it to you and share it with you. We will be afraid of what you have found, for if you do not, the sultan will bring you to us and we will hand you over to him so that he may kill you." When he heard their words, he was amazed and said: You have fallen into everything I was wary of. Then they said: Young man, by God, you cannot conceal what you have found, and do not think that your situation will be hidden. So Yamlikha did not know what to say to them or what to return to them, and he was so afraid that he could not give them an answer.

When they saw that he did not speak, they took his cloak and put it around his neck, then they led him through the streets of the city, chained, until everyone in it heard about him, and it was said: A man who had a treasure was taken. The people of the city, young and old, gathered around him, and they began to look at him and say: By God, this young man is not from this city, and we have never seen him in it, and we do not know him. So Yamlikha did not know what to say to them, despite what he heard from them. When the people of the city gathered around him, he was afraid and remained silent and did not speak. If he had said that he was from the city, he would not have been believed. He was certain that his father and brothers were in the city, and that his ancestors were from the city, and that they would come to him if they heard. He was certain that since the evening before he had known many of its people, and that today he did not know anyone from its people.

While he was standing there, confused, waiting for some of his people, his father or some of his brothers, to come to him and rescue him from their hands, they kidnapped him and took him to the two leaders of the city and its administrators who were running its affairs. They were two righteous men, one of whom was named Arius, and the other was named Astius. When he took him to them, Yamlikha thought that he was taking him to Decius. The tyrant, their king from whom they had fled, began to look right and left, and the people began to mock him, as one mocks a madman or a confused person. So Yamlikha began to cry, then raised his head to the sky and to God, then said: O God, God of the heavens and the earth, infuse with me a spirit from You today to support me with it against this tyrant. And he began to cry and say to himself: Separate me from my brothers. I wish they knew what I have suffered, and that I am being taken to the tyrant Decius.

If they knew, they would come and we would all stand before Decius, for we had pledged to be together, not to disbelieve in God or associate anything with Him, and not to worship tyrants besides God. Separate me from them, for they will never see me and I will never see them, and we had pledged Surat al-Kahf 18:19 And thus We raised them up that they might ask one another. One of them said, "How long have you remained?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city and let him see which of them has the best food, and let him bring you provision." From him,
h
and let him be gentle

and not let anyone know about you. never to be separated in life or death. I wish I knew what he will do to me? Will he fight me or not? That is what Yamlikha himself was saying to his companions when he returned to them.

When he came to the two righteous men, Arius and Aestius, and when Yamlikha saw that he had not taken him to Decius, he came to and stopped crying. Arius and Aestius took the paper and looked at it and were amazed by it. Then one of them said: Where is the treasure that you found, young man? This paper testifies that you have found a treasure. Yamlikha said to them: I did not find a treasure, but this paper is the paper of my fathers, and the inscriptions and minting of this city. But by God, I do not know what is the matter with me, and I do not know what to say to you. Then one of them said to him: Who are you? Yamlikha said to him: I do not know, for I thought that I was from the people of this village. They said: Who is your father and who knows you by it?

c: So he told them
m: the name of his father, but they did not find anyone who knew him or his father. Then one of them said to him: You are a lying man, you do not tell us the truth. Yamlikha did not know what to say to them, but he lowered his eyes to the ground. Some of those around him said to him: This is a madman.

x: Some of them said: He is not mad, but he is deliberately fooling himself in order to escape from you. One of them said to him, looking at him with intense eYa-Sin 36:Do you think that if you act crazy we will send you and believe you that this is your father’s money, and that he struck and engraved this paper more than three hundred years ago? You are only a young boy and you think you can fool us, while we are unkempt, as you can see, and around you are the nobles of the city and its rulers. I think that I will pass by you and you will be severely tortured, then I will tie you up until you confess to this treasure that you have found. When he said that, Yamlikha said: Tell me something I will ask you about, for if you do, I will tell you the truth about what I have. Have you seen King Decius who was in this city yesterday evening, what did he do? The man said to him: There is no man on the face of the earth named Decius, and there was only a king who died a long time ago, and many centuries died after him.

Then Yamlikha said to him: By God, I am perplexed, and no one will believe what I say. By God, I know that we fled from the tyrant Decius, and I saw him yesterday evening when he entered the city of Ephesus, but I do not know whether this city is Ephesus or not. So go with me to the cave in Mount Panglaos, and I will show you my companions. When Arius heard what Yamlikha was saying, he said: O people, perhaps this is a sign from the signs of God that He has bestowed upon you through the hands of this young man. So go with us with him so that he may show us his companions as he said. So Arius and Astius went with him, and the people of the city, great and small, went with them towards the people of the cave to see them. When the young men of the cave saw that Yamlikha had withheld their food and drink from the amount he used to bring, they thought that he had been taken and taken to their king, Decius, from whom they had fled.

While they were thinking that and fearing it, they heard voices and the noise of horses ascending towards them, and they thought that they were messengers of the tyrant Decius sent to them to bring them. When they heard that, they rose to pray, and greeted one another, and advised one another, and said: Let us go and bring our brother Yamlikha, for he is now in the hands of the tyrant Decius, waiting for you to come to him. While they were saying this, and they were sitting in the cave, they saw none but Arius and his companions standing at the door of the cave, and Yamlikha preceded them, so he entered upon them while he was crying, and when they saw him crying they cried with him, then they asked him about his condition, so he told them his story and narrated to them the whole story, and they knew then that they had been asleep by the command of God all that time, and they had only been awakened to be a sign to the people, and to confirm the resurrection, and to know that the Hour is coming without a doubt, then Arius entered after Yamlikha, and he saw a coffin of copper sealed with a silver ring, so he stood at the door of the cave, then he called some of the great men of the city, and he opened the coffin with them, and they found in it two lead tablets, written on them a book, so he read them and found in them: That Maksalmina, and Muhsalmina, and Yamlikha, and Martonus, and Kastunus, and Burus, and Icarnus, and Itibyunus, and Qalus, were young men who fled from Their king Decius the tyrant, fearing that he would tempt them away from their religion, so they entered this cave.

When he was informed of their location, he ordered the cave to be blocked off with stones. We have written down their affair and the story of their report, so that those who come after them may know it if they find them. When they read it, they were amazed and praised God who showed them a sign of the resurrection in them. Then they raised their voices in praise and glorification of God. Then they entered the cave to the youths and found them sitting between its backs, their faces shining, their clothes not worn out. Arius and his companions fell down in prostration and praised God who showed them a sign of His signs. Then they spoke to one another, and the youths informed them of what they had suffered from their king Decius, that tyrant from whom they had fled. Then Arius and his companions sent a messenger to their righteous king, Theodosius, saying: “Hurry, perhaps you will see a sign of God’s signs, which God has made for your kingdom, and made it a sign for the worlds, so that it may be for them a light and radiance, and a confirmation of the resurrection.

So hurry to the youths whom God has resurrected, and they had died more than three hundred years ago.” When the report reached King Theodosius, he rose from the chair he was on, and his mind and reason returned to him, and his concern left him, and he returned to God Almighty, and said: I praise You, O God, Lord of the heavens and the earth, I worship You, and I praise You, and I glorify You, You have been generous to me, and have had mercy on me with Your mercy, so why? When the people of the city heard of this, they rode to him and went with him until they came to the city of Ephesus. The people of the city met them and went with him until they climbed towards the cave until they came to it. When the youths saw Tydosius, they rejoiced at him and fell prostrate on their faces. Tydosius stood before them, then embraced them and wept while they were sitting before him on the ground, praising and thanking God, and saying: By God, you are no more like the disciples when they saw Christ.

He said: May God relieve you, as if you were called and then raised from the graves. The youths said to Tydosius: We bid you farewell with peace, and peace be upon you and the mercy of God. May God protect you and protect your kingdom for you in peace. We seek refuge for you in God from the evil of the jinn and mankind. So he ordered a life of debauchery and disgrace. The worst thing that can be in a person’s belly is that he does not know anything except honor if he is honored with it, and humiliation if he is humiliated with it. While the king was standing, they returned to their beds and slept, and God took their souls by His command. The king rose up to them, put his clothes on them, and ordered that each man of them be given a golden coffin. When evening came and he slept, they came to him in a dream and said: We were not created from gold or silver, but we were created from dust and to dust we shall return, so leave us as we were in the cave on the dust until God raises us from it.

So the king ordered that a coffin be made of teak, and they put them in it. When they left them, God concealed them with terror, so that no one was able to enter upon them. The king ordered that their cave be made into a mosque in which to pray, and he made for them a great festival, and ordered that it be visited every year. This is the story of the People of the Cave. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubayd bin Umair, who said: God sent them, meaning the young men of the Cave, and a Muslim king had been given power over them, meaning over the people of their city, and God had given power over the young men with hunger. One of them said, ‘How long have you stayed?’ They said, ‘We have stayed a day or part of a day.’ He said: “They referred the knowledge of that to God. “They said, ‘Your Lord knows best how long you have stayed.

So send one of you with this silver coin of yours to the city.’” And with them was silver coin of the king who was in his time. Let him bring you provision from him, meaning food. And let no one know about you. So one of them went out and saw the landmarks hidden until he reached the city. The people met him and he did not recognize any of them, so he went out and they did not recognize him, until he reached the one who had the food, and he offered him his food. The one who had the food said, Bring your silver coin. So he brought him the silver coin, and he said, Where did you get this silver coin from? He said: This is our paper and the paper of the people of our country. He said: This paper is far from me. So-and-so, son of so-and-so, struck it three hundred and nine years ago. You have found a treasure, and I will not leave you until I present you to the king. So he presented it to the king, and behold, the king was a Muslim and his companions were Muslims.

He was happy and cheerful, and revealed his affair to them, and told them the report of his companions. So they sent for the tablet in the treasury, and brought it, and it agreed with what he had described of their affair. The polytheists said: We have more right to them, for they are the sons of our fathers. The Muslims said: We have more right to them, for they are Muslims than us. So they went with him to the cave. When they came to the door of the cave, he said: Leave me so that I may enter upon my companions so that I may give them good report, for if they see you with me, you will terrify them. So he entered and gave them good report, and God took their souls. He said: God blinded them to their place, so they were not guided. The polytheists said: We will build a structure over them, for they are the sons of our fathers, and we will worship God in it. The Muslims said: We have more right to them, they are more deserving of us, we will build a mosque for them in which we pray and worship God.

The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of the one who said: God the Most High raised them from their sleep so that they might ask each other questions, as we have explained before, because God the Almighty informed His servants thus in His Book, and God caused the people whom He had caused them to stumble upon them, so that they might realize that God had raised these young men from their sleep after a long period of time in the same state as they were on the day they slept, and they had not aged over the days and nights, and they had not aged over the passage of time and ages in them, and that He has the power to raise from their graves those He caused to die in this world to the place of resurrection on the Day of Resurrection, because God the Almighty informed us of that, and said: And thus We caused them to stumble upon it, that they might know that the promise of God is true and that there is no doubt about the Hour.
The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement:
h
Then send one of you with this money of yours

. The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Iraqis read it as with this money of yours with a fatha on the waw and a kasra on the ra’ and qaf. The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it with a silent Ra and a kasra on the Qaaf.

Some of the Meccans read it with a kasra on the Ra and the assimilating the Qaaf into the Kaaf. All of these readings have the same meanings, because the words differ, and they are well-known dialects of the speech of the Arabs. However, the origin of that is the opening of the Waw and the kasra of the Ra and the Qaaf, because it is the paper, and everything else is included in it to seek lightness. There is also another dialect, which is the paper, as the liver is called Kabd. If that is the origin, then the reading with it is more amazing, without the other two being proven to be correct. We have mentioned the narration that the one who sent the paper with him to Medina was called Yamlikha.

c: Ubayd God bin Muhammad al-Zuhri told me:
m: We are Sufyan, on the authority of Muqatil:
h
Then send one of you with this money of yours
. His name is Yamlikh. As for his saying,
h
So let him see which of them has the best food
, the people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of it.

x: Some of them said: Its meaning is, so let him see which of the people of the city has the Surat al-Kahf 18:19 And thus We raised them up that they might ask one another. One of them said, "How long have you remained?" They said, "We have remained a day or part of a day." They said, "Your Lord knows best how long you have remained. So send one of you with this silver of yours to the city and let him see which of them has the best food, and let him bring you provision." From him,
h
and let him be gentle
and not let anyone know about you. most food.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Which food is the purest? He said: The most.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: similarly, except that he said: Which verse is more?

x: Others said: Rather, it means, O you who make food lawful.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: Which food is the purest? He said: It is permissible.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: similarly.

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: O you who have the best food.
Who said that?

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement: the best food, he said: the best food. The first of the sayings that is most correct in my opinion is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: It is more permissible and purer, and that is because there is no meaning in choosing the one who has the most food to buy from except in the sense that if he has the most food, then it is appropriate for him to have the best of it. He found, and if he stipulated that the person in charge should buy from the owner of the best, then he has been ordered to buy the best, whether what the buyer has of it is little or much of the best, and the interpretation of purer is directed to the most, because he found the Arabs saying: So-and-so’s money has become plentiful: if it has become plentiful, and as the poet said: Our tribes are seven and you are three, and seven is better and more pleasant than three. Meaning: more, and if that is the case, then the good lawful, even if little, is more than the bad unlawful, even if it is much. And it was said, So let him look, which of them, was added to the metaphor of the city, and what is meant by it is its people, because the interpretation of the statement is: So let him look, which of its people has the best food, so that the listener knows what is meant by the statement. And it may be possible that they meant by their saying, Which of them has the best food, which is the most lawful, because they had left their people and they were people of idols, so they did not consider it permissible to eat their slaughtered meat. His saying, Then let him bring you provision from him, means: Let him bring you sustenance from him that you may eat, and food that you may eat.

c: As Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair,
m: Then let him bring you provision from Him. He said: Food. His saying,
h
And let him be gentle
, means: let him be gentle in what he buys, and in his way and entry into the city. And let no one know about you, means: let no one among the people know about you.

evidence.text: While they were saying this, and they were sitting in the cave, they saw none but Arius and his companions standing at the door of the cave, and Yamlikha preceded them, so he entered upon them while he was crying, and when they saw him crying they cried with him, then they asked him about his condition, so he told them his story and narrated to them the whole story, and they knew then that they had been asleep by the command of God all that time, and they had only been awakened to be a sign to the people, and to confirm the resurrection, and to know that the Hour is coming without a doubt, then Arius entered after Yamlikha, and he saw a coffin of copper sealed with a silver ring, so he stood at the door of the cave, then he called some of the great men of the city, and he opened the coffin with them, and they found in it two lead tablets, written on them a book, so he read them and found in them: That Maksalmina, and Muhsalmina, and Yamlikha, and Martonus, and Kastunus, and Burus, and Icarnus, and Itibyunus, and Qalus, were young men who fled from Their king Decius the tyrant, fearing that he would tempt them away from their religion, so they entered this cave.
When they read it, they were amazed and praised God who showed them a sign of the resurrection in them.
The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement: Then send one of you with this money of yours.
The majority of the reciters of Medina and some of the Iraqis read it as with this money of yours with a fatha on the waw and a kasra on the ra’ and qaf.
The majority of the readers of Kufa and Basra read it with a silent Ra and a kasra on the Qaaf.
Some of the Meccans read it with a kasra on the Ra and the assimilating the Qaaf into the Kaaf.
If that is the origin, then the reading with it is more amazing, without the other two being proven to be correct.

x: And his saying, If they gain the upper hand over you, they will stone you, they mean by that: Decius and his companions. They said: If Decius and his companions gain the upper hand over you and know where you are, they will stone you, insulting you with words.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding his statement, If they gain victory over you, they will stone you, they will insult you verbally, they will harm you. And His statement, or they return you to their religion, means: or they return you to their religion, so that you become disbelievers by worshipping idols. And you will never succeed then, means: and you will never attain success, which is eternal survival and immortality in Paradise. So: that is, if you return to their religion forever: during the days of your life.

x: God Almighty says: And just as We raised them after their long sleep, in the same state they were in when they slept, so that they might question one another, and increase in insight into the greatness of God’s power, and in knowledge of the goodness of God’s defense of His friends. Thus did We find them. He says: Thus did We make known to the other group who were in doubt about God’s ability to revive the dead, and in doubt about the creation of the bodies of His creation, in the same state they were in on the day He took them after decay, so that they might know that God’s promise is true, and be certain that the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And thus We made them known, meaning: We made them known so that whoever disbelieves in this hadith may know that the promise of God is true, and that there is no doubt about the Hour. And His statement,
h
When they disputed among themselves their affair

, means: those who found the youths. God Almighty says: And thus We caused these people of Theodosius, who differed about the establishment of the Hour and God’s revival of the dead after their death, to stumble upon them, when they disputed among themselves about what God will do with those of His servants whom He destroyed, and then destroyed them in their graves after their death. Did He create them or did someone else create them? And His statement, And they said, ‘Build over them a structure,’ means: Those whom We made find the people of the cave said, Build over them a structure. “Their Lord is most knowing of them,” means: The Lord of the youths is most knowing of the youths and their condition. And His statement,
h
Those who prevailed in their affair said

, God Almighty says: The people who prevailed in the affair of the people of the cave said, Let us build over them a mosque. And there is disagreement about those who said this statement. Are they the group of Muslims, or are they the infidels? We have mentioned some of that previously, and we will mention, God willing, what has not been mentioned of it.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Those who prevailed in their affair said
, ‘Let us build a mosque over them.’ He said: He meant their enemy.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, who said:
m: God blinded those who made them stumble upon the People of the Cave, and they were not guided. The polytheists said: We will build a building over them, for they are the sons of our fathers, and we will worship God in it. The Muslims said: Rather, we have more right to them, they are more than us. We will build a mosque over them in which we will pray and worship God in it.

x: God Almighty says: Some of those who delve into the matter of the young men of the Cave will say: They are three, and their dog is the fourth.
Some of them will say: They are five, and their dog is the sixth.

i: Guessing at the unseen means: casting suspicion with no certain knowledge, as the poet said:
x: And make me the truth, hidden and hidden And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
They will say
, ‘Three, their dog being the fourth.’ And
h
they will say
, ‘Five, their dog being the sixth.’ Guessing at the unseen: meaning slandering at the unseen.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, casting on the unseen, he said: casting on suspicion. And His statement: And they say, ‘Seven, and their dog is the eighth,’ meaning: And some of them say: They are seven and their dog is the eighth. Say, ‘My Lord knows best their number.’ meaning: The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say these statements about the number of the youths from the People of the Cave, guessing from the unseen: “My Lord knows best their number. None knows them.” He says: None knows their number except a few of His creation.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
None knows them except a few
, meaning: a few people.

x: Others said: Rather, by little he meant the People of the Book.
Who said that?

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
None knows them except a few
. He said: He means the People of the Book. Ibn Abbas used to say: I am one of those whom God has excepted, and he used to say: Their number is seven.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
None knows them except a few
. He said: I am one of the few, they were seven.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: he mentioned to us that Ibn Abbas used to say: I am one of those few whom God excepted, they were seven and the eighth of them was their dog.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said:
m: Ibn Abbas said: Their number is seven and the eighth of them is their dog, and I am one of those whom God excepted.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding His statement:
h
None knows them except a few
, he said: Ibn Abbas used to say: I am one of the few, they are seven and the eighth of them is their dog. And His statement:
h
So do not dispute about them except with an outward dispute

, the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So do not dispute, O Muhammad, meaning: Do not argue with the People of the Book about them, meaning about the number of the People of the Cave, and the number was omitted because it is sufficient to mention them in it so that the listeners will know what is meant. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement:
h
So do not dispute about them

, he said: Do not dispute about their number. And His statement: Except for an outward dispute, the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the outward dispute that God excepted and permitted for His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace.

x: Some of them said: It is what God has related in His Book, and it is permissible for him to recite to them, and he should not dispute with them about anything other than that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement:
h
So do not dispute about them except with an outward dispute
means: What I have told you is sufficient,
h
so do not dispute about them

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
So do not dispute about them except with an outward dispute
. He said: Except with what we have shown you about their affair.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
So do not dispute about them except with an outward dispute
: that is, what we have told you about their affair is sufficient for you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
So do not dispute about them
, he said: It is enough for you what we have told you about their affair.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
So do not dispute about them except with an outward dispute
, meaning: What we have told you is sufficient.

x: Others said: The outward dispute is to say: It is not as you say, and similar statements.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement: except for an apparent argument, he said: That he says to them: It is not as you say, you do not know their number.

x: If they say such and such, then say it is not like that, for they do not know their number.
h
They will say
, ‘Three, their fourth being their dog,’ until he reached guessing at the unseen.
And His statement:
h
And do not consult any of them about them

, God Almighty says: And do not consult any of the people of the Book about the number of the youths from the Companions of the Cave, meaning any of them from the People of the Book, because they do not know their number, and they only speak about them guessing at the unseen, not with certainty of the statement. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not consult anyone of them about them
, he said: They are the People of the Book.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And do not consult anyone of them about them
from the Jews.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And do not ask any of them about them: from the Jews. He said: And do not ask the Jews about the matter of the People of the Cave, except what I have told you about their matter.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: h
And do not consult anyone of them about them

: from the People of the Book, we were told that they were the sons of Rukna - and Rukna: the kings of the Romans - God granted them Islam, so they were unique in their religion, and they isolated themselves from their people, until they reached the cave, then God struck their deafness, so they remained for a long time until their nation perished and a Muslim nation came after them, and their king was Muslim.

x: This is a lesson from God Almighty to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. He commanded him not to be certain that whatever happens will inevitably happen, unless he attributes it to God’s will, because nothing happens except by God’s will. And it was said to him that, as we have heard, because he promised those who asked him about the three questions that we mentioned previously, one of which was the question about the matter of the young men of the Cave, that he would answer them tomorrow, and he did not make an exception. So the revelation was withheld from him, as it was said, for that reason for fifteen days, until its delay saddened him. Then God revealed to him the answer about them, and He made known to His Prophet the reason for the withholding of the revelation from him, and taught him what he should use in his preparations and informing him about what would happen of the matters that had not been revealed to him from God.

So He said: “And do not say, O Muhammad, about anything, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ as you said to those who asked you about the matter of the People of the Cave, and the questions they asked you about, ‘I will tell you about them tomorrow,’ unless God wills.” The meaning of the statement is: unless you say with it, ‘God willing.’ So He left out mentioning ‘you say’, being satisfied with what was mentioned from it, since there was an indication of it in the statement. Some Arabists said: It is possible that the meaning of his saying: Except if God wills is an exception from the saying, not from the action. Its meaning, according to him, was: Do not say a saying except if God wills that saying. This is a view far removed from the apparent meaning of the revelation, while it contradicts the interpretation of the people of interpretation.
And his saying:
h
And remember your Lord when you forget
The people of interpretation differed regarding its meaning.
Some of them said: And make an exception in your oath if you remember that you forgot that during the oath.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Harun al-Harbi told us: Naim bin Hammad told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding a man who swears an oath. He said to him: He should make an exception, even if it is for a year. He used to say:
h
And remember your Lord when you forget
. It was said to al-A’mash about that: I heard it from Mujahid. He said: Layth bin Abi Salim told me about it. He thinks that this cloak of mine is gold.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Jaʿfar, on the authority of Al-Rabiʿ, on the authority of Abu Al-ʿAliyah,
m: regarding his statement: “
h
And never say of anything
, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ except [if] God wills.
h
And remember your Lord when you forget
,” the exception, then you remember, so repeat.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And remember your Lord when you forget
, he said: It has reached me that Al-Hasan said: If he remembers that he did not say: God willing, then let him say: God willing.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: Remember your Lord when you disobey.
Who said that?

c: Nasr bin Abdul Rahman told me: Hakam bin Salm told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: regarding the statement of God,
h
And remember your Lord when you forget
, he said: Remember your Lord when you disobey.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Sinan, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: something similar. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: Its meaning is: Remember your Lord if you neglect to remember Him, because one of the meanings of forgetfulness in the speech of the Arabs is abandonment, and we have explained that previously.

x: Is it permissible for a man to exaggerate in his oath, since the meaning of the words is what I mentioned after a period of time from the state of his oath?

Rather, the correct thing is for him to excite himself even after he has broken his oath, and say: God willing? So that he may get out of what he said of what God has obligated him to do in this verse, and the hardship is removed from him by his leaving what he was commanded to say of that. As for the expiation, it is not removed from him in any case, unless his excitation is connected to his oath.

What is the meaning of the statement of the one who said to him: I will repeat it even after a year, and the one who said to him that even after a month, and the statement of the one who said as long as he is in his seat?

Their meaning in that is similar to our meaning in that it is for him, even after ten years, and that by his seeking forgiveness and saying, God willing, after a while after the state of his oath, the hardship that would have been binding on him if he had not said it is removed from him. As for the expiation, it is binding on him if he breaks his oath in any case, unless his seeking forgiveness was connected to the oath, and that is because we do not know of anyone who said that to him the second time after a while claiming that that removes the expiation from him if he breaks his oath. In that is the clearest evidence for the correctness of what we said in that, and that the meaning of the statement in it was similar to our meaning in it. And His statement, And say, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer than this in right conduct,’ the Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, Perhaps God will guide me and make me steadfast in what I promised you and informed you would happen, if He wills.

It has been said: This is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say if he forgot to make an exception in his speech, which he had in mind regarding a future matter, along with his saying: God willing, if he remembered.
It was mentioned that he said this:

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad,
m: a man from Kufa, who used to interpret the Qur’an, and Yahya ibn Abbad used to sit with him. He said: “
h
And never say of anything
, ‘I will do that tomorrow,’ except, ‘If God wills.’
h
And remember your Lord when you forget

and say, ‘Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer than this in right conduct.’” He said: So why does a person forget to say, If God wills? He said: So his repentance from that, or the expiation for that, is to say, Perhaps my Lord will guide me to something nearer than this in right conduct. Surat al-Kahf 18:24 Except if God wills.
h
And remember your Lord when you forget
and say, "Perhaps my Lord will guide me to a nearer right course than this."

x: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of His statement:
h
And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine

Some of them said: That is report from God Almighty about the People of the Book that they say that as well, and they cited as evidence for the correctness of their statement His statement: Say, God knows best how long they stayed. They said: If that were report from God about the extent of their stay in the cave, then His statement: Say, God knows best how long they stayed would not have had any comprehensible meaning, and God has informed His creation of the extent of their stay in it and its extent.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement:
h
And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine
, this is the statement of the People of the Book, so God rejected it from them and said: “Say: God knows best how long they remained. To Him belong the unseen of the heavens and the earth.”

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they remained in their cave
, he said in the wording of Ibn Masoud, and they said: And they remained, meaning that he said the people, do you not see that he said, Say, God knows best how long they remained.

c: Ali bin Sahl told us: Damrah bin Rabi’ah told us, on the authority of Ibn Shawdhab, on the authority of Matar al-Warraq,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And they remained in their cave
for three hundred years. He said: It is something that the Jews said, so God rejected it and said: “Say: God knows best how long they remained.”

x: Others said: Rather, it is report from God about the amount of time they stayed in their cave.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Damru told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine
. He said: The number of years they remained.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: in a similar manner, and he added to it: “Say: God knows best how long they stayed.”

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Abi Rawad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubaid bin Umair, who said:
m: h
And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine
. He said: And nine years.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq,
m: something similar.

c: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told us: Abu Usamah told us: Al-Ajlah told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, who said:
m: This verse was revealed:
h
And they remained in their cave
for three hundred years. They said: Days, months, or years? So God revealed: Years, and they added nine.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
And they remained in their cave
, he said: between two mountains.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. And the most correct of the sayings in this regard is to say as God Almighty said: And the companions of the cave remained in their cave, asleep until God resurrected them, so that they might question one another, and until someone made them stumble, for three hundred and nine years.

c: And that is because God informed us
m: of that in His Book. As for what was mentioned about Ibn Masʿud that he read and said:
h
And they remained in their cave

and the saying of the one who said that is from the saying of the People of the Book, and God has rejected that from them, then its meaning in that, God willing, was that the People of the Book said, as mentioned during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the youths from the time they entered the cave until our day were three hundred and nine years, so God rejected that from them, and informed His Prophet that that was the amount of their remaining in the cave from the time they took refuge in it until He sent them so that they might ask each other questions, then the Most High said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad: God knows best how long they remained after He took their souls, after He sent them from their sleep until this day, and no one knows that except God, and other than the one whom God informed of that.

x: What indicates that that is the case?

The evidence for that is that He, may His praise be glorified, began the report about the length of their stay in their cave, saying, And they stayed in their cave for three hundred years, and they increased by nine. And He Surat The Cave: 25
h
And they remained in their cave for three hundred years and added nine

. did not provide evidence that this was report from Him about what some people said, and it is not permissible for His report about something to be added to it being report about something else without proof, because if that were permissible, it would be permissible in all of His report, and if that were permissible in His report, it would be permissible in the report of others to be added to it that it is His report, and that is the reversal of the essence of the truths and what is not imagined to be corrupt.

If someone thinks that His statement, Say, 'God knows best how long they stayed' is evidence that His statement, And they remained in their cave is a report from Him about a people who said it, then that would have to be the case if it could not be interpreted otherwise. But since it is possible, as we said, that its meaning is: Say, 'God knows best how long they stayed until the day We revealed this surah', and similar meanings, then it is not necessary for that to be evidence that His statement,
h
And they remained in their cave is a report from God about a people who said it
. And if there is no evidence for that, and no report has come that His statement,
h
And they remained in their cave is a report from God about a people who said it

, and no proof has been established that must be accepted, then what we said is correct, and what contradicts it is invalid. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement, three hundred years.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians, read it as three hundred years with a tanween on the word three hundred, meaning: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years. The majority of the reciters of the people of Kufa read it as three hundred years with the addition of three hundred to the years, without a tanween. The first of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the correct reading of the one who reads it three hundred with the tanween years, and that is because the Arabs only add the hundred to what explains it if its explanation comes with the word of one, and that is like their saying three hundred dirhams, and I have a hundred dinars, because the hundred and the thousand are a large number, and the Arabs do not explain that except with what is in its meaning in the large number. The singular is used for the genus, but this is not the case for a small number, because the Arabs may have put a small plural in place of a large number, but this is not the case for a large number.
However, if its interpretation comes in the form of a plural, then it is given a tanween, so you say: I have a thousand dirhams, and I have a hundred dinars, as I have described. And His statement,
h
To Him belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth

, the Most High says: To God belongs the knowledge of the unseen of the heavens and the earth. Nothing of it escapes Him, and nothing is hidden from Him. He says: So submit to Him a knowledge that extends to the time the youths remained in the cave until this day of yours, for no one knows that except He who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that is none other than God, the One, the Prevailing. And His statement, He sees and hears it, He says: He sees and hears with God, and that is in the sense of exaggeration in praise, as if it were said: He did not see and hear. The interpretation of the statement: God sees everything that exists and hears everything that is heard.
Nothing of that is hidden from Him.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: I see and hear with Him. So no one sees or hears more than God, Blessed and Exalted be He.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “He sees and hears them.
h
They have no protector besides Him
,” he said: He sees their deeds and hears that from them, All-Hearing, All-Seeing. And His statement,
h
They have no protector besides Him

, means, may His praise be glorified: His creation has no protector besides their Lord who created them, who oversees their affairs and their management, and directs them in what they are directed to. And He does not associate anyone with His judgment, meaning, God does not make anyone a partner in His judgment and His judgment of His creation other than Him. Rather, He is the One who is alone in judgment and judgment over them, and in their management and direction as He wills and loves.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of his statement, three hundred years.

The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians, read it as three hundred years with a tanween on the word three hundred, meaning: And they remained in their cave for three hundred years.
The majority of the reciters of the people of Kufa read it as three hundred years with the addition of three hundred to the years, without a tanween.

The first of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the correct reading of the one who reads it three hundred with the tanween years, and that is because the Arabs only add the hundred to what explains it if its explanation comes with the word of one, and that is like their saying three hundred dirhams, and I have a hundred dinars, because the hundred and the thousand are a large number, and the Arabs do not explain that except with what is in its meaning in the large number.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And follow, O Muhammad, what has been revealed to you of this Book of your Lord, and do not abandon its recitation, and following what is in it of God’s commands and prohibitions, and acting according to what He has permitted and forbidden, lest you be among the lost. That is because the fate of those who disobey Him and abandon following Him on the Day of Resurrection will be Hell. There is no changing His words. He says: There is no changing what He has promised with His words that He has revealed to you, the people of His disobedience, and those who act contrary to this Book that We have revealed to you. And His statement,
h
And you will not find any refuge besides Him

, means: If you, O Muhammad, do not recite what was revealed to you from the Book of your Lord, and follow it and fulfill it, then you will be met with the threat of God in which He threatens those who transgress His limits.

You will not find any refuge besides God to which you can turn and a place of refuge to which you can turn, because God’s power encompasses you and all of His creation. None of them is able to escape from a matter that He intends for you. And similar to what we said about the meaning of his saying retreating, the people of interpretation said, even though their words differed in explaining it.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement, in refuge, he said: a refuge.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Multahidan he said: refuge.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And you will not find any refuge besides Him
. He said: A refuge.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, in refuge, he said: a refuge and no shelter.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And you will not find any refuge besides Him

, he said: They will not find any refuge to seek, nor will they find any shelter besides Him, nor anyone to protect them. And Multahid is the plural of lahd, from which it is said: Lahdat ila kadha if you incline towards it, and from which the word hadd is called lahd, because it is on one side of the grave, and not the crack in the middle of it, and from which comes ilhad in religion, which is obstinacy in turning away from it and abandoning it.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And be patient, O Muhammad, with your companions who call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening, remembering Him with glorification, praise, declaration of His oneness, supplication, and righteous deeds, such as the obligatory prayers and others. They desire, by doing that, His countenance, not worldly gain. We have mentioned the difference of opinion among those who differed in his statement, “
h
They call upon their Lord in the morning and the evening

” in Surat Al-An’am, and the correct statement in this regard according to us is that it is sufficient to repeat it in this place. The reciters read this as in the morning and the evening. It has been mentioned about Abdullah bin Amir and Abu Abdul Rahman Al-Sulami that they used to recite it as in the morning and the evening. This is a reading that is disliked by the people of knowledge of Arabic, because ghudwah is a definite noun, and there is no alif or lam in it, because only what is not definite is known by the alif and lam, as for definite nouns, they are not known by them.

And further, ghudwah is not added to anything, and its prevention from addition is clear evidence of the prevention of the alif and lam from entering it, because what the alif and lam enters from the nouns is suitable for addition, as the Arabs say: I came to you in the morning of Friday, but they do not say: I came to you in the morning. Friday, and the reading according to us in this is what the reciters in the countries do, so we do not permit anything else due to their consensus on that, and for the reason that we explained from the aspect of Arabic. And His saying,
h
And let not your eyes pass beyond them

, the Most High is saying to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not turn your eyes away from those whom I have commanded you, O Muhammad, to be patient with, to others of the infidels, and do not go beyond them to him. Its origin is from their saying: I went beyond that, so he went beyond it.
And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement,
h
And let not your eyes pass beyond them
, he said: Do not go beyond them to others.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
And let not your eyes pass beyond them
, meaning: Do not pass beyond them to others.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And keep yourself patient

... the verse, he said: The people said to the Prophet in: We are too shy to sit with so-and-so and so-and-so and so-and-so, so avoid them, O Muhammad, and sit with the nobles of the Arabs, then the Qur’an was revealed: “
h
And keep yourself patient
with those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His countenance.
h
And let not your eyes pass beyond them
