So when he was prostrating when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, God extracted his arrogance from the prostration, so He cursed him and postponed him until the Day of Judgment. He said: Ibn Abbas said: His statement,
h
He was from the jinn
, is that he was called Paradise because he was its keeper, just as a man is called a Meccan, a Medinan, a Kufan, or a Basran. Ibn Jurayj said this.

x: Others said: They are a tribe of angels, a tribe, and the name of his tribe was the jinn.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Salih,
m: the freed slave of Al-Tawamah, and Sharik Ibn Abi Namir, one of them or both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Among the angels is a tribe of jinn, And Iblis was among them, and he used to rule what was between heaven and earth, but he disobeyed, so God became angry with him and transformed him into a cursed devil. May God curse him as he was transformed. He said: If a man’s sin was due to arrogance, then do not expect him. But if his sin was due to disobedience, then expect him. Adam’s sin was due to disobedience, and Iblis’ sin was due to arrogance.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, “
h
And when We said to the angels

, ‘Prostrate to Adam,’ and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was one of the jinn,” is a tribe of angels called the jinn. Ibn Abbas said: If he had not been one of the angels, he would not have been commanded to prostrate, and he was in Surat al-Kahf 18:50
h
And when We said to the angels

, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated, except for Iblis. He was of the jinn, and he disobeyed the command of his Lord. Then would you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are to you an enemy? An evil exchange for the wrongdoers. charge of the treasury of the lowest heaven. He said: Qatada used to say: He went crazy from obeying his Lord. Al-Hasan used to say: God forced him to return to his lineage.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Except Iblis,
h
he was from the jinn
, he said: He was from a tribe of angels called the jinn.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said:
m: Iblis was never among the angels for even a moment, and he is the origin of the jinn, just as Adam, peace be upon him, is the origin of mankind.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Ubaid told us:
m: I heard Ad-Dahhak say: Iblis was over the lowest heaven and over the earth and the keeper of Paradise.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, So they prostrated themselves, except for Iblis,
h
he was from the jinn

, Ibn Abbas used to say: Iblis was from the noblest of the angels and the most honorable of their tribe, and he was the guardian of Paradise, and he had authority over the lowest heaven and authority over the earth, and among the things that his soul suggested to him from the decree of God was that he saw that he had honor over the people of the heavens, so arrogance occurred in his heart that no one knows except God, so God extracted that arrogance from him when He commanded him to prostrate to Adam, but he was arrogant and was from the disbelievers, so that is what He said to the angels, Indeed, I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what you reveal and what you conceal, meaning: what Iblis concealed in his soul of arrogance. And his saying,
h
He was from the jinn
, Ibn Abbas used to say: God said,
h
He was from the jinn
, because he was a keeper of the heavens, just as a man is called a Meccan, a Medinan, a Basran, or a Kufan.

x: Others said: The name of Iblis’ tribe was the jinn, and they are a tribe of angels called the jinn, so God Almighty said,
h
He was from the jinn
, so He attributed him to his tribe.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Saʿid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
He was from the jinn
, he said: From the jinn who work in the gardens.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Saeed Al-Yahmadi Ismail bin Ibrahim told us: Suwar bin Al-Ja’d Al-Yahmadi told us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab,
m: regarding his statement, of the jinn, he said: Iblis was one of the jinn whom the angels expelled, so some of the angels captured him and took him to heaven.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement, Except Iblis, he was one of the jinn and disobeyed the command of his Lord, he said: He was the keeper of Paradise, so he was called Paradise.

c: Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi told me: Ahmad ibn Bashir told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Abi al-Miqdam, on the authority of Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said:
m: Iblis was one of the keepers of Paradise. We have already explained the statement on this in what has preceded in this book of ours, and we have mentioned the differences of opinion among those who differed on it, so that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. And His statement,
h
So he disobeyed the command of his Lord

, means: So he went against the command of his Lord, deviated from it and deviated, as Ruʿbah said: They wander in Najd and are deeply wicked and unjust. A: By fawasiq means: the camels that deviate from the straight path of Najd, and likewise, fawasiq in religion is only deviation from the straight path and deviation from righteousness. It is narrated from the Arabs by hearing: Fawasiq means that the date fawasiq means that it came out of its shell, and fawasiq means that the mouse fawasiq means that it came out of its hole.

x: Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: Fawasiq ‘an amr Rabbih was said because it means that he fawasiq means that he rejected the command of God, just as the Arabs say: Atakhmat ‘an al-ta’im meaning: I was gorged on eating. We have already explained the statement about that, and that its meaning is: He deviated and went against the command of God, and deviated from it.

Some scholars of the Arabic language said: The meaning of fawasiq is excessiveness. He claimed that the Arabs say: Fawasiq fi al-nafqah means that he was excessive in it. He said: The fasiq was called fasiq because of his excess in what God has forbidden. And the scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Omar told us, and he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty,
h
Then he disobeyed the command of his Lord
, he said: Regarding prostration to Adam. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Mujahid narrated: Concerning His statement,
h
Then he disobeyed the command of his Lord
, he said: He disobeyed in prostrating to Adam. And His statement,
h
Then would you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are enemies to you

? God Almighty says: “O children of Adam, would you take him who was arrogant towards your father and envied him and denied My blessings upon him, and deceived him until I expelled him from Paradise and the comfort of his life therein to the earth and the hardship of life therein, and you obey him and his descendants instead of God despite his enmity towards you in the past and present, and you abandon the obedience of your Lord who bestowed blessings upon you and honored you by making His angels prostrate to your father, and making him dwell in His gardens, and giving you from the abundance of His blessings what cannot be counted in number?” And the temptation of Iblis: the devils who tempt the children of Adam.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Will you then take him and his offspring as allies instead of Me? He said: His offspring are the devils, and he counted them as: Zalnabur, the master of the markets, who would place his banner in every market between heaven and earth, and Thabar, the master of calamities, and the one-eyed, the master of fornication, and Masut, the master of report, who would bring it and throw it into the mouths of the people, and they would find no basis for it, and Dasim, who, if a man entered his house and did not greet him and did not mention God, would see the goods that were not raised, and if he ate and did not mention the name of God, he would eat with him.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Hafs bin Ghiyath told us, he said:
m: I heard Al-A’mash say: If I enter the house and I have not converted to Islam, I see a woman who is ablution, so I say: Lift up, lift up, and I argue with them, then I remember and say: Dasim Dasim.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They are four: Thabr, Dasim, Zalnabur, Al-Awar, and Masut: one of them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Do you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me? And they reproduce as the children of Adam reproduce, and they are your enemies.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Then would you take him and his descendants as allies instead of Me while they are enemies to you

? He is the father of the jinn just as Adam was the father of mankind. And he said: God said to Satan: I will not create for Adam any descendants except that I will create for you the like thereof. So there is no one among the children of Adam who does not have a devil attached to him. And His statement,
h
What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers

, the Almighty says: What an evil exchange for the disbelievers in God is to take Iblis and his offspring as allies instead of God, and they are your enemies because they abandoned taking God as an ally by following His commands and prohibitions, and He is the One who bestowed blessings upon them and upon their father Adam before them, and bestowed upon them countless favors, as an exchange. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said:
m: Thanayzid, he said: Thanasa’id, on the authority of Qatada:
h
What an evil exchange for the wrongdoers
! What an evil exchange! They exchanged the worship of their Lord for obeying Satan.

x: The Almighty said: I did not make Iblis and his offspring witness the creation of the heavens and the earth meaning: I did not make them witness that so that I could seek their help in creating them nor the creation of themselves meaning: I did not make some of them witness the creation of some of them so that I could seek their help in creating them, rather I was unique in creating all of that without any helper or supporter, meaning: So how did they take their enemy as allies instead of Me, while they are a creation of the likes of their creation, and they abandoned My worship while I am the One who bestowed favors upon them and upon their ancestors, and their Creator and the Creator of those whom they befriend instead of Me, alone in that without any helper or supporter. His saying, And I would not have taken those who lead astray as helpers, means: I would not have taken those who do not guide to the truth, but rather lead astray, so whoever follows them deviates from the straight path, as helpers and supporters.
It is from their saying: So-and-so supports so-and-so if he strengthens and aids him.
Some of the interpreters said something similar.
Who said that?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And I would not have taken the misguiders as assistants: meaning, helpers.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: something similar. What he meant by that is that Satan and his followers lead the children of Adam astray from the truth and do not guide them to the right path. It may also be possible that he meant the misguiders who are followers in misguidance and companions who are not guided.

x: God the Almighty says: And on the Day when He will say God the Almighty to those who associate others with Him, Call upon My partners whom you claimed He will say to them: Call upon those whom you claimed were My partners in worship to support you and protect you from Me. So they called upon them, but they did not respond to them He says: So they sought help from them, but they did not help them.
h
And We placed between them a place of destruction
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of that.
Some of them said: Its meaning is: And We placed between these polytheists and what they used to call upon besides God, partners in this world, enmity on that Day.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told me: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: regarding the statement of God, And We have placed between them a cause of destruction, he said: He has placed enmity between them on the Day of Resurrection.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Uthman ibn Umar told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And We placed between them a cause of destruction
. He said: Enmity.

x: Others said: Its meaning is: And We made their action a cause of destruction for them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And We placed between them a cause of destruction
, he said: a cause of destruction.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, destructive, he said: destruction.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And We placed between them a cause of destruction
, he said: The cause of destruction is the destroyer, in which some of them destroyed others, some of them destroyed others. And he recited: And We have set a time for their destruction.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad bin Yazid, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Mubqan means destruction.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Urfajah,
m: regarding His statement,
h
And We placed between them a place of destruction
, he said: a place of destruction.

x: Others said: It is the name of a valley in Hell.
Those who said that were mentioned:

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, on the authority of Amr al-Bakali:
m: And We placed between them a barrier. He said: A deep valley that separated the people of misguidance from the people of guidance, and the people of Paradise from the people of Hell.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
And We placed between them a barrier of destruction

. It was mentioned to us that Amr al-Bakali told on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, he said: It is a deep valley through which the people of guidance will be separated on the Day of Resurrection from the people of misguidance.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Omar bin Ubaid told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Artah, he said:
m: Mujahid said, And We placed between them a barrier, he said: A valley in the Fire.

c: Muhammad bin Omar told us, and he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
And We placed between them a place of destruction
, he said: A valley in Hell.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: his example.

c: Muhammad bin Sinan al-Qazzaz told me, he said: Abd al-Samad told us, he said: Yazid bin Dirham told us, he said:
m: I heard Anas bin Malik say regarding the statement of God Almighty, And We have placed between them a place of destruction, he said: A valley in Hell of pus and blood. The most correct of the statements about that is the valley that we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and those who agreed with him in the interpretation of the place of destruction: It is the destroyer, because the Arabs say in their speech: Qad awbaqt so-and-so: if they destroyed him. And from this is the saying of God the Almighty: Or destroy them for what they have earned: meaning: destroy them. And it is said about the destroyer himself: Qad wabaq so-and-so, so he is yawbaq and baqa. And the language of Banu Amir: yabaq without a hamza. And it was narrated from Tamim that they say: yabaq. Surat al-Kahf 18:52 And the Day He will say, "Call upon My partners whom you claimed." So they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and We will place between them a barrier of destruction. And it was narrated and baqa yabaq and baqaan, narrated by Al-Kisa’i. And some of the scholars of the speech of the Arabs from Basra used to say: the destroyer is the appointed time, and he cites the saying of the poet as evidence for his saying that: And the evil of the curtain did not leave any shame for him, and the two valleys were ruined. And he interprets it as an appointment. It is possible that the destroyer that God Almighty made between these polytheists is the valley mentioned by Abdullah bin Amr. It is possible that it is the enmity that Al-Hasan said.

x: And His statement, And the criminals will see the Fire, means: And the polytheists will see the Fire on that day, and they will think that they will fall into it, meaning: They will know that they will enter it.

c: As Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And they thought that they would fall upon it
, he said: They knew.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Diraj, on the authority of Abu al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The disbeliever sees Hell and thinks that it will be his destination from a distance of forty years. And His statement, And they will not find any way out of it, means: And they will not find any way out of the Fire that they saw, to which they could turn away, meaning: They will not find any way out of its destination, because God has decreed that upon them. And from the meaning of detour in the sense of direction is the statement of Abu Kabir al-Hudhali: Azharhal about the gray hair of the bank or is there no immortality for the one who is generous and burdensome

x: The Almighty says: And We have certainly given people examples in this Qur’an from every example, and We have admonished them in it from every admonition, and We have presented arguments against them in it with every argument so that they may remember and repent, and take heed and be admonished, and be deterred from what they are committed to of associating partners with God and worshipping idols. And man is most disputatious of all things. He says: And man is most disputatious and contentious of all things, neither repenting to the truth nor being deterred by admonition.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And man is most disputatious of anything

, he said: Dispute is quarrel, the quarrel of the people with their prophets, and their disdain for what they brought. And he recited: This is nothing but a human being like you; he eats of what you eat and drinks of what you drink. And he recited, he wants to do you a favor. And he recited until he died... the verse, And if We sent down to you a book on paper, the verse. And he recited, And if We opened to them a gate from heaven and they continued therein to ascend, he said: They are not you, they would have said, “Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people affected by magic.”

x: The Almighty says: What prevented these polytheists, O Muhammad, from believing in God when guidance, the statement of God, came to them, and they knew the truth and reality of what you are calling them to, and from seeking forgiveness for what they are continuing in of their polytheism, except that they came upon Our way with their likes from the nations who denied their messengers before them, or that the punishment had come to them before.
The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that, and some of them said: Its meaning is:
h
or the punishment comes to them suddenly
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement,
h
Or the punishment comes to them suddenly
, he said, suddenly.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. And others said: Its meaning is: Or the punishment comes to them clearly.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Or the punishment comes to them face to face
, he said: Face to face is seeing that face. The reciters differed in the reading of that, so a group of people read it,
h
Or the punishment comes to them face to face

, with a damma on the qaf and the ba’, meaning that there will come to them from the punishment various types and kinds, and they directed the face to the plural of qabil, just as the slain is pluralized as qatil, and the new is jadida.

x: Another group read,
h
Or the punishment comes to them face to face

, with a kasra on the qaf and a fatha on the ba’, meaning or the punishment comes to them visibly, from their saying: I spoke to him face to face. I have explained the statement about that in Surat Al-An’am in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of that, so a group of people read it, Or the punishment comes to them face to face, with a damma on the qaf and the ba’, meaning that there will come to them from the punishment various types and kinds, and they directed the face to the plural of qabil, just as the slain is pluralized as qatil, and the new is jadida.

x: The Almighty says: We do not send Our messengers except to give good tidings to the people of faith and belief in God of His great reward in the Hereafter. And to warn the people of disbelief in Him and denial of His great punishment and painful torment, so that they may desist from associating partners with God, and refrain from disbelieving in Him and His sins. And those who disbelieve argue with falsehood to refute thereby the truth. He says: And those who disbelieved in God and His Messenger argue with falsehood, like their saying to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell us about the story of the young men who went away at the beginning of time and it was not known what happened to them, and about the man who reached the easts and wests of the earth, and about the spirit, and what is similar to that of which they used to argue with him, seeking to bring him down, out of contempt for him, may God bless him and grant him peace.

So God said to them: We do not send Our Messengers to you for argument and disputes, but rather We send them as bearers of good tidings to the people of faith of Paradise, and as warnings to the people of disbelief of the Fire, and you argue with them with falsehood, seeking from you thereby to invalidate the truth that My Messenger brought to you. And He meant by His saying to refute thereby the truth to invalidate thereby the truth and remove it and go away with it. It is said from it: to refute something means if it disappears. And he went, and it is said: This is a place of ruin: meaning a slippery place in which neither a hoof nor a foot can stay.

i: From this comes the saying of the poet:
x: I replied and Naji Al-Yashkari was careful and cautious, as a camel deviated from refutation.

It is narrated: And he dismissed it, and I refuted it: if I removed it and invalidated it. And His statement, And they took My signs and that with which they were warned in ridicule, means: And the disbelievers in God took His proofs with which He argued against them, and His Book which He sent down to them, and the warnings with which He warned them in ridicule, mocking them, saying that this is nothing but legends of the ancients which He wrote down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening, and If We willed, We could have said the like of this.

The Almighty says: Who among people is more prone to turning away and rejecting in the wrong place than he who reminds him of His signs and proofs, guiding him with them to the path of guidance and guiding him with them to the way of salvation, but he turns away from His signs and proofs, by which he can deduce salvation from destruction. And he forgets what his hands have put forth. He says: And he forgets what he has done before of destructive sins, so he does not repent or turn back.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us,
m: then: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And he forgot what his hands had put forth, meaning he forgot what had gone before of sins. And His statement, Indeed, We have placed coverings over their hearts, lest they understand it, and in their ears, deafness, God Almighty says: We have placed coverings over the hearts of those who turn away from the signs of God when they are reminded of them, lest they understand it, because the meaning is that they understand what they are reminded of. And His statement, and in their ears, deafness, means: in their ears, a weight, lest they hear it. And if you call them to guidance, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if you, O Muhammad, call these people who turn away from the signs of God when reminded of them, to steadfastness on the path of truth and belief in God and what you have brought them from your Lord, they will never be guided then, meaning: they will never be steadfast on the truth, and they will never believe in what you have called them to, because God has sealed their hearts, their hearing, and their sight.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And your Lord is the Concealer, O Muhammad, of the sins of His servants by His forgiveness of them if they refuse them. The Possessor of Mercy towards them. If He were to punish them for what they have earned, these people who turn away from His signs when they are reminded of them for what they have earned of sins and crimes, He would have hastened the punishment for them. But out of His mercy towards His creation, He does not do that to them until their appointed time and their appointed terms. Rather, they have an appointed time.

But they have an appointed time, and that is the appointed time for their punishment, which is the Day of Badr. They will not find any refuge besides it. God Almighty says: These polytheists will not find, even if He does not hasten the punishment for them in this world other than the appointed time that He has made a appointed time for their punishment, a refuge to which they can resort, and a place of safety with which they can escape.
He means that they will not find a fortress in which they can be detained from God’s punishment. It is said from this: And I went from such and such to such and such, “Athal and Uwala,” like Uwala.

i: And from this is the saying of the poet: If you leave yourself to the public, you will not speak He says:
x: No, she was saved, and Al-A’sha said: I may make the master of the house forget me, and he may be wary of me, but he will not be able to do so.
In the same way as we said about that, the people of interpretation stood up.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement a refuge he said: a place of refuge.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
They will not find any refuge besides Him
: he says: a refuge. Bashar said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
h
They will not find any refuge besides Him
: meaning they will not find any protector or refuge besides Him.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement,
h
They will not find any refuge besides Him
, he said: There is no refuge besides Him to which they can resort.

x: God Almighty says: And those cities of 'Aad and Thamud and the companions of the thicket, We destroyed their people when they were unjust, so they disbelieved in God and His signs, And We appointed for their destruction an appointed time meaning a time and a deadline, when they reached it a punishment came to them and We destroyed them with it. He says: So likewise We appointed for these polytheists from your people, O Muhammad, who will never believe in you an appointed time, when that appointed time came to them We destroyed them? Our way with those who came before them of their likes.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
For their destruction is an appointed time
, he said: a term.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told me, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, for their destruction. The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as for their destruction with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the lam, referring it to the source of the verb ahlakawa ikhlakan. Asim read it as for their destruction with a fatha on the meem and lam, referring it to the source of the verb halakawa hilakan and mahlakaan. The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of the one who read it as for their destruction with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the lam, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it, and based on the statement, And those towns, We destroyed them, so it is more appropriate for the source to be from ahlakana, since it had come before it. It was said: We destroyed them, and he had said before, and those towns, because destruction only befell the people of the towns, so he returned to the meaning, and the speech was based on it, not the wording.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He said, And those villages, We destroyed them when they wronged, meaning their people, just as he said, And ask the village, and he did not use the word villages, but he applied the word to the people, and applied the word in the village to it until he said, in which we were. And he said, We destroyed them, and he did not say, We destroyed it? He applied it to the people, just as he said, Tamim came, and he attributed the verb to Banu Tamim, and he did not attribute it to Tamim. If he had done that, he would have said, Tamim came, and this is not good in something like this, because he intended something other than Tamim in something like this, so he made it a noun, and he did not accept, if it is defective, that what precedes it be deleted entirely, the meaning of the ta’ from came with Banu Tamim, and he left the verb as it was so that it would be known that something before Tamim had been deleted.

Some of them said: It is permissible to say: Those villages, We destroyed them, because the village took the place of the people, so it is permissible to refer to the people once and to it once. This is not permissible in the case of Tamim, because the tribe is known by it, and Tamim is not the tribe, but rather the tribe is known by it. If the tribe had been named after the man, it would have been applied to him, just as you say: It occurred in Hud, meaning in Surat Hud, and Hud is not the name of the surah, but rather the surah is known by it. If the surah had been named Hud, it would not have been applied. So you would have said: It occurred in Hud, O man, and it would not have been applied. Likewise, if Banu Tamim had been named Tamim, it would have been said: This is Tamim who has arrived. So the interpretation of the statement is: And those villages, We destroyed them when they were unjust, and We appointed a time for their destruction.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, for their destruction.
The majority of the reciters of Hijaz and Iraq read it as for their destruction with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the lam, referring it to the source of the verb ahlakawa ikhlakan.
Asim read it as for their destruction with a fatha on the meem and lam, referring it to the source of the verb halakawa hilakan and mahlakaan.

The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of the one who read it as for their destruction with a damma on the meem and a fatha on the lam, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it, and based on the statement, And those towns, We destroyed them, so it is more appropriate for the source to be from ahlakana, since it had come before it.

x: The Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, when Moses, son of Imran, said to his servant Joshua, I will not cease, meaning, I will not cease to walk until I reach the junction of the two seas.

c: As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement,
h
I will not leave

, he said: I will not stop. And it was said: What he meant by his statement, the meeting of the two seas, is the meeting of the Persian Gulf and the Roman Sea. And the meeting is a noun from their statement, to gather by gathering.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr told us,
m: Qal’a: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, until I reach the junction of the two seas. The two seas are the Persian Gulf and the Roman Sea. The Roman Sea is to the west, and the Persian Sea is to the east.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, the meeting place of the two seas, he said: the Persian Gulf and the Roman Sea.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: The congregation of the two seas. He said: The Roman Sea and the Persian Gulf, one of them is before the east, and the other is before the west.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The meeting place of the two seas.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya ibn al-Durais told us: Abu Ma’shar told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b,
m: regarding his statement,
h
I will not leave until I reach the junction of the two seas

, he said: Tangier. And his statement, Or I will travel for ages, he said: Or I will travel for a time and an age, and it is one. The plural of both its long and short forms is: ahqaab. And the Arabs would say: I was with him for a period of time, and they would pluralize it as ahqaab.

x: Some of the Arabists interpreted his statement,
h
I will not leave

, as meaning I will not move, and he cited as evidence for that statement the verse of al-Farazdaq. They did not leave until their women were walking in the valley of Dhi Qara'ib al-Lata'im. He says: They are still there.
Some scholars of Arabic speech said that the word haqb in the language of Qais means year. As for the interpreters, they say what I will mention about it, which is that they differed about it.
Some of them said: It is eighty years.
Who said that?

c: It was narrated on the authority of Hisham,
m: who said: Abu Balj narrated to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Amr, who said: Al-Haqb is eighty years.

x: Others said: It is seventy years.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: Or I spend ages, he said: Seventy autumns.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. And others said something similar to what we have said.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, Or shall I pass on for ages, he said: an age.

c: Ahmad bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, periods, he said: Periods are a period of time.

c: Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: Or I pass an age, he said: An age is time.

x: He, the Most High, means: When Moses and his servant reached the junction of the two seas, as:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Between the two of them, he said: between the two seas.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly. And his saying,
h
They forgot their fish
, he means by his saying they forgot: they left.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
h
They forgot their fish
, he said: They led him astray.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: They led him astray.

x: Some of the Arabists said: The whale was with Joshua, and it was the one who forgot him, so forgetfulness was attributed to them, as He said: From them come forth pearls and coral, and it only comes forth from the salt, not the fresh. It is permissible for me to say they forgot because they had both prepared provisions for their journey, so one of them carrying it was added to the fact that it was carried by them, just as it is said: The people left from such and such a place, and they carried with them such and such provisions, and only one of them carried it, but since it was their opinion and their command, it was attributed to all of them. Likewise, if its carrier forgets it in a place, it is said that the people forgot their provisions, so it is attributed to all of them because of its carrier’s forgetting it, so the speech applies to all of them, and the action is from one, so it is the same in His statement
h
they forgot their fish
, because God Almighty addressed the Arabs in their language, and in the speech they know among themselves.

As for His statement and from them came forth pearls and coral, then the statement about that according to us is contrary to what He said about it, and we will explain it, God willing, when we come to it. As for His statement
h
and it took its way in the sea
, a swarm, it means that the fish took the path it took in the sea, a swarm.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: h
So he took his way in the sea

, a tunnel. He said: The whale took. And what is meant by the tunnel is the path and the way, he travels in it: he goes in it and follows it. Then the scholars differed about the description of his path in the sea as a tunnel.

x: Some of them said: His path that he travels on becomes like a stone.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said:
m: Ibn Abbas said, his statement a path he said: Its trace was like a stone.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ubay ibn Ka’b, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he mentioned the hadith of that: “No water has been created since people were other than it. The place of the fish in it remained and was created like a window until Moses returned to it and saw a path, so he said: That is what we were seeking.”

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Atiyah told us, he said: Amr ibn Thabit told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So he took his way in the sea
, a tunnel, he said: He came and saw the trace of his wings in the mud when he fell into the water. Ibn Abbas said,
h
So he took his way in the sea
, a tunnel, and he flew with his hand.

x: Others said: Rather, his path in the sea became solid water.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: A path of ploughs passed through until it reached the sea, then it traveled, and it did not take a path in it except a hard, solid path.

x: Others said: Rather, its path in the sea became a rock.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The whale did not touch anything in the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock.

x: Others said: Rather, it only took its path on land to the water, until it reached it, not in the sea.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
And it took its way in the sea

, a swarm, he said: He said: The whale was gathered in the valley after its death when God revived it. Ibn Zayd said: Abu Shuja’ told me that he saw it. He said: I brought it and it was a split whale with one eye, and another split in which there was nothing. The correct statement about that is to say as God the Almighty said: And the whale took its way in the sea, a swarm. It is possible that that swarm was due to its disappearance from the land, and it is possible that it was due to the freezing of the water, and it is possible that it was due to its transformation into a stone. The most correct statement about it is what was narrated about it from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, which we mentioned from Abu from him.

x: God Almighty says: So when they had passed Moses and his servant, the junction of the two seas, Moses said to his servant, Joshua, “Bring us our lunch,” meaning: We brought our lunch and gave it to him, and he said: Bring us our lunch, as it is said: The lunch came and I brought it, like he went and I made it go away, We have certainly suffered from this journey of ours, meaning: We have certainly suffered from this journey of ours hardship and fatigue, and Moses said that, as mentioned, after he had passed the rock, when hunger was cast upon him, so that he would remember the fish and return to the place of his request.

God the Almighty says: The servant of Moses said to Moses when he said to him: Bring us our lunch so that we may eat: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish there? And none made me forget to mention it except Satan. He says: And none made me forget to mention it except Satan, that I should mention it. So an is in the accusative case in response to the fish, because the meaning of the statement is: And none made me forget to mention the fish except Satan. The fish preceded the action, and his saying that I should mention it responded to it. It has been mentioned that this is in the copy of Abdullah: And none made me forget to mention it except Satan.

c: Bishr told me that.
m: He said: Yazid told us. He said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada.

c: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me that
m: he heard Muhammad bin Muqal narrating on the authority of his father that the rock that Moses took refuge in was the rock that was below the River of the Wolf on the road. And he took his way into the sea, astonishing. He was amazed by it.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, In the sea is a wonder, he said: Moses was amazed by the trace of the whale in the sea and its circles in which it disappeared, and he found greenness there.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
And he took his way in the sea
, astonishingly, so when Moses took his way in the sea, astonishingly, he was amazed by the school of whales.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And it took its course in the sea, astonishing, he said: By God, it is amazing, a whale that was eaten for ages. What is more amazing than a whale that was eaten for ages, then it became clear until it was gathered into the sea?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: The whale did not touch anything in the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was amazed by that.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Al-Hasan bin Atiyah told us, he said: Amr bin Thabit told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: h
And he took his way in the sea
as a wonder. He said: meaning, the school of whales in the sea was a wonder for Moses.

x: God Almighty says: So Moses said to his servant, That meaning: your forgetting the fish. What we were seeking meaning: what we were seeking and asking for, because Moses was told, Your companion whom you want is when you forget the fish.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
That is what we were seeking
, Musa said: That was when I was informed that I would find Khidr when the fish escaped me.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: similarly, except that he said: Where the fish leaves me. And His statement,
h
So they returned
, following their footsteps, means:
h
So they returned
on the path they had traveled, turning back, following the footsteps they had taken. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, stories, he said: Moses and his servant followed the trace of the whale, and they parted the sea, returning.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So they returned

, following their footsteps, he said: Moses and his servant followed the traces of the whale in splitting the sea, and Moses and his servant were returning, and Moses was amazed by the traces of the whale in the sea, and the circles in which it disappeared.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: They returned to their original state, and they returned to their footsteps, retracing their steps.

c: Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told me, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ubay ibn Ka’b, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in his statement,
h
That is what we were seeking
h
So they returned
, following their footsteps, retracing their footsteps, meaning they followed their footsteps until they reached the entrance of the fish.

x: And His saying,
h
And they found one of Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us
, means: We granted him mercy from Us.
h
And We taught him knowledge from Us
, means: We taught him knowledge from Us as well.

c: As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: From Us is knowledge: meaning from Us is knowledge. The reason for Moses and his servant’s journey, and his meeting with this scholar whom God mentioned in this place, is that Moses was asked, Is there anyone on earth who is more knowledgeable than you? He said, No, or his soul told him that, and he disliked that for him. So God wanted to inform him that there are among His servants on earth those who are more knowledgeable than him, and that it was not for him to impose something on him that he had no knowledge of, but that he should have left that to his scholar.

x: Others said: Rather, the reason for that was that he asked God, may He be glorified and praised, to guide him to a scholar who would increase his knowledge to his own knowledge.

Who said that? Ibn Humayd narrated: Yaqub narrated on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Moses asked his Lord and said: O Lord, which of Your servants is most beloved to You? He said: He who remembers Me and does not forget Me. He said: Which of Your servants is most just? He said: He who judges with truth and does not follow desire. He said: O Lord, which of Your servants is most knowledgeable? He said: He who seeks the knowledge of people for his own knowledge, perhaps he may find a word that will guide him to guidance or turn him back from ruin. He said: O Lord, is there anyone on earth? He said: Yes. He said: O Lord, who is he? He said: Al-Khidr. He said: Where can I look for him? He said: On the shore near the rock from which the fish escapes. He said: So Moses went out looking for him, until what God had mentioned happened, and Moses reached him at the rock, and each of them greeted the other, and Moses said to him: I want you to accompany me.

You will not be able to bear my company. He said: Yes. He said: Then if you accompany me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you. So they set out. When they embarked on the ship, he made a hole in it. He said: Have you made a hole in it to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my affair with hardship. So they set out. When they met a boy, he killed him. He said: Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: So Moses' statement about the wall was for himself, and to seek something from this world, and his statement about the ship and the boy was for God, "He said: This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience."

c: So he told him what he said
m: about the ship, the boy, and the wall. He said: So he sailed with him in the sea until he reached the meeting place of the seas, and there is no place on earth with more water than it. He said: And your Lord sent the swallow, and it began to draw water from it with its beak. It was said to Moses: How much water do you think this swallow has drawn from this water? He said: How little it has drawn! He said: O Moses, my knowledge and your knowledge in comparison to God's knowledge is as much as this swallow has drawn from this water. Moses had thought to himself that there was no one more knowledgeable than him, or spoke about it, so from that he was commanded to go to Al-Khidr.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: Moses addressed the Children of Israel and said: No one knows more about God and His command than I do. So God revealed to him to go to this man.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: that it was said to him: A sign of your meeting with Him is that you forget some of your belongings. So he and his servant Joshua bin Nun went out and took provisions from a salted fish, until when they were where God willed, God restored the soul to the fish, so it sailed into the sea. The fish took its path through the sea, and sailed into it. “So when they had passed, he said to his servant, ‘Bring us our breakfast. We have certainly encountered fatigue on this journey of ours.’” Until he reached and took its course in the sea in a wondrous way. So Moses took his course in the sea in a wondrous way, and he was amazed by the school of fish. Al-Hasan narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Muammar narrated: Abu Ishaq narrated: Saeed bin Jubair narrated: Ibn Abbas said: When Moses followed the traces of the fish, he came to a man lying down with his garment covered over him. Moses greeted him, but the man uncovered his face and returned his greeting, saying: Who are you? He said: Moses. He said: The companion of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: Did you not have any business with the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, but I was commanded to come to you and accompany you. He said: You will not be able to have patience with me, as God related, until he reached When they embarked on the ship, the companion of Moses tore it open. He said: Have you tore it open to drown its people? You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot, and do not burden me with my task with hardship. So they set off, until they met a boy, and he killed him. He said: Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? Abu Kuraib narrated: Yahya ibn Adam narrated: Sufyan narrated: Amr ibn Dinar narrated: Saeed ibn Jubayr narrated: I said to Ibn Abbas: Nawwaf claims that Al-Khidr was not the companion of Moses. He said: The enemy of God has lied! Ubayy ibn Ka’b narrated: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated: Moses stood up among the Children of Israel as a preacher and it was said: Who is the most knowledgeable of people? He said: I am. God rebuked him when he did not attribute the knowledge to Himself. He said: Yes, he is a servant of Mine at the confluence of the two seas. He said: O Lord, what about him? It was said: You take a fish and put it in a basket. Then he said to his servant: If you lose this fish, tell me. So they set out walking along the seashore until they came to a rock. Moses lay down, and the fish stirred in the basket, so it came out and fell into the sea. Then God stopped the flow of water from it, so it became like a vault, and the fish became a swarm, and it was a wonder to them. Then they set out. When it was time for the next day, Moses said to his servant: Bring us our lunch, for we have certainly encountered fatigue in this journey of ours. Moses did not find fatigue until he had passed where God had commanded him. He said: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the fish, and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan, and it took its way into the sea, a wonder. He said: He said: That is what we were seeking. So they returned, following in their footsteps. He said: They were following in their footsteps. He said: They came to the rock, and there was a man sleeping, covered with his garment. Moses greeted him, and he said: How can I bring peace in our land? He said: I am Moses. He said: Moses of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes. He said: O Moses? I have knowledge from the knowledge of God, which God taught me and you do not know, and you have knowledge from His knowledge which He taught you and I do not know. He said: Then I will follow you on the condition that you teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you. So they set off walking along the shore, and Al-Khidr recognized him, so he carried him without a rope. Then a bird came and landed on a seashore and pecked, or pecks, in the water. Al-Khidr said to Moses: My knowledge and your knowledge have not decreased from the knowledge of God except to the extent that this bird has pecked or pecks in the sea. Abu Jaʿfar Al-Tabari is uncertain, and in his book he pecks. He said: While he was there, nothing surprised Moses except that he was sticking a peg or pulling out a mattress from it, so Moses said to him: We carried him without a rope and you are tearing it apart to drown its people? You have certainly done something terrible. He said: Did I not tell you that you would not be able to have patience with me? He said: Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot. He said: The first time Moses forgot. He said: Then they went out and walked, and they saw a boy playing with the boys, so he took him by the head and killed him. Moses said to him: Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? You have certainly done a horrible thing. He said: Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said: If I ask you about anything after this, do not accompany me, for you have received an excuse from me. He said: So they set out until they came to the people of a town, and they asked its people for food, but they did not find anyone to feed them or give them water. They found a wall about to collapse, so he straightened it with his hand. He said: He wiped it with his hand. Moses said to him: They did not host us nor did they lodge with us. If you had wanted, you could have taken payment for it. He said: This is parting between me and you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said:

c: I wish he had been patient until he told us
m: their stories.
b.via: I wish he had been patient until he

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ammarah, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, who said:
m: I was sitting and Ibn Abbas leaned on him, and there were a group of the People of the Book with him.

x: Some of them said: O Abu Al-Abbas, Nawwaf, the son of Ka’b’s wife, claims on the authority of Ka’b that Moses, the prophet who sought knowledge, was in fact Moses bin Misha. Saeed said: Ibn Abbas said: Does Anoof say this? Saeed said: I said to him: Yes, I heard Nawwaf say that. He said: Did you hear him, O Saeed? He said: I said: Yes. He said: Nawwaf lied. Then Ibn Abbas said: My father bin Kaab told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Moses, the prophet of the Children of Israel, asked his Lord Surat al-Kahf 18:65 Then they found one of Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him knowledge from Us. and said: O Lord, if there is one among Your servants who is more knowledgeable than me, then show me him. He said to him: Yes, among My servants is one who is more knowledgeable than you. Then He described his place to him and gave him permission to meet him.

So Moses went out with his young man and with him a beautiful whale. It was said to him: If this whale revives in a place, then your companion is there and you have fulfilled your need. So Moses went out with his young man, and with him was that whale carrying him. He walked until he was exhausted from walking, and he reached the rock and that water, the water of life. Whoever drinks from it will live forever, and nothing dead comes near it except that it will come to life. So when they descended and the whale touched the water, it revived and took its path in the sea, a tunnel, so they set off. When they passed its turning point, Moses said: Bring us our lunch. We have certainly encountered fatigue in this journey of ours. The young man said and mentioned: Did you see when we took refuge at the rock? I forgot the whale, and nothing made me forget it except Satan, I mention it and took his way in the sea, amazingly.

Ibn Abbas said: Moses appeared on the rock when they reached it, and if a man wrapped in his cloak, Moses greeted him, and the scholar responded to him, then he said to him: What brought you? If you have a job among your people? Moses said to him: I have come to you to teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will never be able to have patience with me. He was a man who knew the unseen and knew that.
Yes. He said: And how can you have patience over that of which you have no knowledge?

That is, you only know the outward appearance of what you see of justice, and you have not encompassed the knowledge of the unseen as I know. He said: You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in any matter. And if you see something that contradicts me, He said: If you follow me, do not ask me about anything. And if I deny it, until I mention it to you. So they set out walking on the shore of the sea, exposing themselves to people, seeking someone to carry them, until a new, secure ship passed by them, the best, most beautiful, and most secure of which no ship had ever passed by. They asked its people to carry them, so they carried them. When they were secure in it and it entered with them with its people, he took out his beak and a hammer, then he went to a part of it and struck it with the beak until it tore. Then he took a board and closed it over it, then he sat on it patching it.

He said: Moses saw a terrible thing, "You have torn it to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing." He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me? He said, Do not hold me accountable for what I forgot. That is, what I left of your covenant. And do not burden me with my affair with hardship. Then they got out of the ship and set off until they came to the people of a town. There were boys playing behind it, among them was a boy who was not more charming, richer, or more radiant than any of the boys. He took him in his hand and took a stone. He said, He struck his head with it until it crushed it and killed him. Moses said, Then he saw a terrible thing that he could not bear, a young boy who had no sin. He said, Have you killed a pure soul without a soul? That is, a young boy without a soul. You have certainly done a terrible thing. He said, Did I not tell you that you would never be able to have patience with me?

He said, "If I ask you about anything after this, do not keep company with me. You have received an excuse from Me." That is, you have been excused for my affair. "So they set off until they came to the people of a town. They asked its people for food, but they refused to host them. They found therein a wall about to collapse, so he demolished it, then sat down to build it. Moses was annoyed by what he saw him doing, being tasked with something he could not be patient with, so he said, If you had wished, you could have taken payment for it. That is, we asked them for food but they did not feed us, and we hosted them but they did not host us, then you sat down without doing anything. If you had wished, you could have been given payment for his work. He said, “This is a parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that over which you could not have patience.” As for the ship, it belonged to poor people working at sea, and I intended to discredit it, but behind them was a king who seized every ship by force.

In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b: Every good ship. I only discredited it to turn him away from it, so it was safe when he saw the defect that had been made in it. “As for the boy, his parents were believers, and we feared that he would overburden them through transgression and disbelief. So we intended that their Lord should substitute for them one better than him in purity and nearer of kinship. And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and beneath it was a treasure belonging to them. Their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord intended that they should reach maturity and extract their treasure as a mercy from your Lord. And I did not do it of my own accord. That is the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.” Ibn Abbas used to say: The treasure was nothing but knowledge.

c: Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan Ibn Ammarah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said:
m: It was said to Ibn Abbas: We have not heard any mention of the youth of Moses in a hadith, and he was with him. So Ibn Abbas said, in what is mentioned of the youth’s hadith: The youth drank from the water and became immortal, so the scholar took him and placed him on a ship, then he sent him into the sea, and it will continue to surge with him until the Day of Resurrection, and that was because he was not allowed to drink from it, so he drank.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: And when Moses said to his boy, ‘I will not cease until I reach the junction of the two seas or I will continue for ages,’ he said: When Moses and his people prevailed over Egypt, he settled his people in Egypt. When they settled in the house, God revealed to him, Remind them of the days of God. So he addressed his people, and mentioned what God had given them of goodness and blessings, and mentioned to them when God saved them from the people of Pharaoh, and mentioned to them the destruction of their enemy, and God had made them successors on earth, and he said: God spoke to your Prophet directly, and chose me for Himself, and sent down upon me love from Him, and God gave you everything you asked of Him, so your Prophet is the best of the people of the earth, and you read the Torah, so he did not leave a blessing that God had bestowed upon them without mentioning it and explaining it to them, so a man from the Children of Israel said to him: They are like that, O Prophet of God, we know what you are saying, so is there anyone on earth more knowledgeable than you, O Prophet of God? He said: No. So God sent Gabriel to Moses, peace be upon them, and said: God says: How do you know where I put my knowledge? Yes, there is a man on the shore of the sea who is more knowledgeable than you. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Moses asked his Lord to show him to him, and God revealed to him: Go to the sea, and you will find a whale on the shore of the sea. Take it and give it to your servant, then stick to the shore of the sea, and if you forget the whale and it perishes from you, then you will find the righteous servant you were looking for. When the journey of Moses, the Prophet of God, became long and he was exhausted, he asked his servant about the whale, and his servant, who was his young man, said to him: Did you see when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the whale, and nothing made me forget to mention it except Satan. The young man said: I saw the whale when it took its way in the sea, forming a swarm. That amazed Moses, so he returned until he came to the rock, and he found the whale thrashing in the sea, and Moses was following it. Moses kept bringing his staff forward, making noise with it. 0About the water following the whale, and the whale made nothing touch the sea except that it dried up until it became a rock, so the Prophet of God was amazed by that until the whale reached an island of the islands of the sea, so he met Al-Khidr there and greeted him, so Al-Khidr said: And upon you be peace, and how can this peace be on this land, and who are you? He said: I am Moses, so Al-Khidr said to him, Am I a companion of the Children of Israel? He said: Yes, so he welcomed him, and said: What brought you? He said: I came to you so that you may teach me from what you have been taught of sound judgment. He said: You will never be able to have patience with me. He said: You will not be able to do that. Moses said: You will find me, God willing, patient, and I will not disobey you in anything. He said: So he went with him and said to him: Do not ask me about anything I do until I explain its matter to you, so that is his saying: Until I cause you to mention it to me. So they got on the ship, intending to land, so Al-Khidr got up and tore the ship, so Moses said to him: You tore it to pieces in order to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement: But when they reached the place where they met, they forgot their fish, it was mentioned that when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, crossed the sea and God saved him from the people of Pharaoh, he gathered the Children of Israel and addressed them, saying: You are the best and most knowledgeable people on earth. God has destroyed your enemy, and has divided the sea for you, and has sent down the Torah to you. He said: It was said to him: There is a man here who is more knowledgeable than you. He said: So he and his servant Joshua bin Nun set out in search of him, and they stocked up on salted fish in a basket of theirs, and it was said to them: If you forget what you have with you, you will meet a knowledgeable man called Al-Khidr. So when they reached that place, God restored the soul to the fish, so it let it escape from the bridge until it reached the sea, then it traveled and did not travel on any path except that it became frozen water. He said: Moses and his servant went on. God Almighty says: “So when they had passed, he said to his servant, ‘Bring us our breakfast. We have certainly suffered on this our journey much fatigue.’ He said, ‘Have you seen when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the fish.’” Then he recited until His saying:
h
And We taught him knowledge from Us

. They met a knowledgeable man called Al-Khidr, and he mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Khidr was called Al-Khidr because he sat on a white fur and it shook green under him.

c: Al-Abbas bin Al-Walid told me: My father told us: Al-Awza’i told us: Al-Zuhri told us, on the authority of Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Mas’ud, on the authority of Ibn Abbas
m: that he and Al-Harbin Qais bin Hisn Al-Fazari had a dispute about the companion of Moses. Ibn Abbas said: He is Al-Khidr. Ubayy bin Ka’b passed by them and Ibn Abbas called him and said: My companion and I have a dispute about the companion of Moses whom he asked about the way to meet. He said: Did you hear the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, mention his affair? He said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: While Moses was with a group of the Children of Israel, a man came to him and said: Do you know of anyone more knowledgeable than you? Moses said: No. So God revealed to Moses: Yes, our servant Al-Khidr. Moses asked about the way to meet him, so God made the fish a sign for him, and it was said to him: If you miss the fish, go back, for you will meet him. Moses was following the traces of the whale in the sea, and Moses’ servant said to Moses: Did you see when we took refuge on the rock? I forgot the whale. Moses said: That is what we were seeking. So they returned, following their traces, and they found our servant Khidr, and what happened to them was what the Scriptures related.

c: Muhammad bin Marzouq told me, he said: Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhan told us, he said: Abdullah bin Omar Al-Numairi told us, on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid, he said:
m: I heard Al-Zuhri narrating, he said: Ubaidullah bin Abdullah bin Utbah bin Masoud told me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he and Al-Har bin Qais bin Hisn Al-Fazari disputed about the companion of Moses. Then he mentioned something like the hadith of Al-Abbas, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka’b, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Surat al-Kahf 18:65 Then they found one of Our servants to whom We had given mercy from Us and had taught him knowledge from Us.

evidence.text: In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka’b: Every good ship.

x: God Almighty says: Moses said to the scholar: Shall I follow you so that you may teach me from the knowledge that God taught you what is guidance to the truth and evidence of guidance.

He said, 'You will never be able to have patience with me.' God Almighty says, "The scholar said, 'You will never be able to have patience with me, because I work with the hidden knowledge that God taught me, and you have no knowledge except the outward aspects of things, so do not have patience with what you see of actions, as we mentioned from the report from Ibn Abbas before that he was a man who worked with the unseen and he knew that."

The Almighty says, informing us about the words of the All-Knowing to Moses: How can you be patient, O Moses, with what you see from me of actions whose correctness you have no knowledge of, and continue with me in them, while you only judge the correctness of the one who is right and the error of the one who is wrong based on what is apparent to you and the extent of your knowledge, and my actions occur without apparent evidence for your own eyes of their correctness, because they begin for reasons that occur later, not immediately, and you have no knowledge of what happened about them, because they are unseen, and you do not encompass the knowledge of the unseen with information? Knowledge.

He said, You will find me, God willing, patient with what I see from you, even if it is contrary to what I think is right, and I will not disobey you in any matter meaning: I will do what you command me to do, even if it is not in accordance with my desires.

The Blessed and Exalted says: The Knower said to Moses: If you follow me now, do not ask me about anything that I know of that you find objectionable, for I have informed you that I do work on the unseen which you do not encompass with knowledge, until I mention to you about it. He says: Until I mention to you what you see of the actions that you find objectionable, I mention them to you and explain their matter to you, and I begin the report about them for you.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: So do not ask me about anything until I tell you about it meaning about something I do until I explain its matter to you.

x: God Almighty says: So Moses and the scholar set out, searching for a ship to board, until they found it and boarded the ship. When they boarded it, the scholar tore the ship apart. Moses said to him: You tore it apart after we had gone into the sea, "to drown its people. You have certainly done a terrible thing." He said: You have certainly done a terrible thing, and you have committed an evil act.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
You have certainly done a most terrible thing

, meaning, amazing. A people have set their ship adrift and it has been punctured, when we are most in need of it. But he knew of that what the Prophet of God, Moses, did not know, from the knowledge of God that He gave him, and He said to the Prophet of God, Moses, peace be upon him, If you follow me, do not ask me about anything until I mention it to you.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
You have certainly done something terrible
, meaning: something strange.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
You have certainly done something terrible
, he said: something reprehensible.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same. And the word imr in Arabic speech means: a calamity, and from it is the saying of the rajaz poet: My peers have purified me from a terrible calamity if I am a woman Some scholars of Arabic speech say: Its root is: everything that is severe and plentiful. It is said that it is said to the al-Nas 114:they have been commanded if they have become numerous and their matter has become severe. He said: The source of it is: the matter, and the noun is: the matter. The reciters differed in the recitation of His statement, to drown its people.
