God the Almighty said: I will make you bear what I carry, I will expand your chest so that it can contain everything, I will expand your understanding so that you will understand everything, I will make your tongue easy for you so that you can speak everything, I will open your hearing so that you will comprehend everything, I will extend your sight so that you will implement everything, I will manage your affairs so that you will master everything, I will count for you so that nothing will escape you, I will protect you so that nothing will escape you, I will strengthen your back so that nothing will guide you, I will strengthen your pillar so that nothing will overcome you, I will strengthen your heart so that nothing will frighten you, I will subject light and darkness to you, so make them soldiers among your soldiers, the light will guide you before you and darkness will surround you from behind, I will strengthen your mind so that nothing will frighten you, I will make what is in front of you easy so that you can attack everything, I will strengthen your step so that you can defeat everything, I will clothe you with awe so that nothing will threaten you. When he was told that, he set out to lead the nation at sunset. When he reached them, he found a crowd and a number that only God could count, and a strength and might that no one could count. He could not bear it except God, and different tongues and scattered desires, and divided hearts. When he saw that, he overwhelmed them with darkness, so he set up three armies around them, and surrounded them from every side, and surrounded them until he gathered them in one place. Then he seized them with light, and called them to God and to His worship.

x: Some of them believed in Him, and some of them turned away. So he went to those who turned away from Him, and he brought darkness upon them, so it entered their mouths, noses, ears, and cavities, and entered their homes and dwellings, and covered them from above them, and from below them, and from every side of them. So they raged in it and were confused. When they feared that they would perish in it, they raged to Him with one voice, so He removed it from them and took them by force, so they entered into his call. So he gathered from the people of the West great nations, and made them one army, then he set out with them leading them, and the darkness drove them from behind them and guarded them from around them, and the light was in front of them leading them and guiding them, and he walked in the right side of the earth, and he He wanted the nation in the right-hand corner of the earth called Hawil, and God made his hand, heart, opinion, mind, sight and command subservient to him, so he did not make a mistake when he commanded, and when he did something he did it perfectly.

So he set out leading those nations and they followed him, and when he reached a sea or a ford, he built ships from small planks like sandals, and he arranged them in an hour, then he put in them all those with him from those nations and those soldiers, and when he crossed the rivers and seas, he split them, then he gave each person a plank so that he would not tire of carrying it, and he continued like that until he reached Hawil, and he worked in them as he would work in a hermit. When he finished it, he went on his way to the right side of the earth until he reached a place of worship at sunrise, and he worked there and recruited soldiers from it, as he had done with the two nations before it. Then he turned back towards the left side of the earth, and he wanted to go to Tawil, which is the nation opposite Hawil, and they are opposite each other, and between them is the entire width of the earth.

When he reached it, he worked there and recruited soldiers from it as he had done with what came before it. When he finished it, he turned from it to the nations in the middle of the earth, from the jinn and the rest of the people, and Yajuj and Majuj. When he was on some of the way, near the end of the Turk towards the east, a righteous nation of mankind said to him: O Dhul-Qarnayn, between these two mountains there are creatures from the creation of God, and many of them are similar to humans, and they are like beasts, they eat grass, and prey on animals and wild beasts as wild beasts prey on them, and they eat the vermin of the earth, all of them snakes and scorpions, and every living thing that God created on the earth. God has not created them to grow in one year, nor increase as they increase, nor multiply as they multiply. If they have a period of time, as we see of their growth and increase, then there is no doubt that they will fill the earth, and expel its people from it and prevail over it and spread corruption in it.

Not a year passes since we have lived with them without us anticipating them and waiting for their first ones to appear to us from between these two mountains. Shall we give you an outlay on condition that you make between us and them a barrier? He said, What my Lord has established me in is better, so help me with strength and I will make between you and them a barrier. Bring back to me the rocks, iron, and copper so that I may explore their lands, learn their knowledge, and measure what is between their two mountains. Then he set out to lead them until he reached them and was in the middle of their country. He found them to be of the same size, male and female. The height of each one of them was like half of a square man among us. They had claws in the place of fingernails on our hands, and molars and fangs like the molars and fangs of wild beasts, and jaws like the jaws of camels, strong.

You could hear them move when they ate, like the movement of a camel’s jug, or like the chomping of an old stallion or a strong horse. They were hardy, with hair on their bodies that covered them and protected them from the heat and cold if they were to befall them. Each one of them had two large ears, one of which was furry on its back and belly. The other is the down of its back and belly, and it covers them both when it is worn, covering itself with one of them and spreading out the other, spending the summer in one of them and wintering in the other, and there is not a male or female among them except that he knows the time at which he will die, and the end of his life, and that is because no male among them dies until a thousand children come out of his loins, and no female dies until a thousand children come out of her womb, so when that happens death is certain, and they are provided with the dragons in the days of spring, and they ask for rain when they are waiting for it as we ask for rain at its time, so they throw one of them every year, and they eat it their entire year until the same of the next year, so it enriches them despite their abundance and growth, so when it rains and they are fertile and live and fat, and its effect is seen on them, then females are born to them, and the males from them are in heat, and if it misses them they become thin and barren, and the males are exhausted and the females dream, and the effect of that is clear on them, and they call each other like doves, and howl like dogs, and copulate wherever they meet Animal mating.

When Dhul-Qarnayn saw that from them, he turned to the area between the two mountain-sides, and measured the distance between them, while he was in the farthest part of the land of the Turks, near the rising of the sun. He found that the distance between them was a hundred farsakhs. When he began his work, he dug a foundation for it until he reached the water, then he made its width fifty farsakhs, and he made its filling rocks, and its clay copper, which was melted and then poured over it, so that it became like a vein of a mountain that the earth was crushing. Then he rose and honored it with iron and molten copper, and made a vein of yellow copper in between it, so that it became like a reddish cloak of the yellowness of copper and the blackness of iron. When he had finished it and perfected it, he set out intentionally towards a group of humans and jinn. While he was traveling, he was brought to a righteous nation who guide with the truth and by it they are just.

He found a nation that was fair and moderate, who divide equally, rule with justice, and are sympathetic and merciful to one another. Their condition is one, their word is one, their morals are similar, their way is upright, and their hearts are united. Their conduct was good, and their graves were at the doors of their houses, and there were no doors on their houses, and there were no princes over them, and there were no judges among them, and there were no rich, nor kings, nor nobles among them, and they did not differentiate between them, nor were they superior to each other, nor did they differ, nor did they quarrel, nor did they abuse each other, nor did they fight, nor did they suffer from drought, nor were they angry, nor were they afflicted with the plagues that afflict people, and they lived the longest lives of people, and there was no poor, nor needy, nor rude, nor coarse among them.

When Dhul-Qarnayn saw that about them, he was amazed by it, and said: Tell me, O people, your story, for I have counted the entire earth, its land and sea, its east and west, its light and darkness, and I have not found anyone like you, so tell me your story. They said: Yes, so ask us whatever you want. He said: Tell me, why are the graves of your dead at the doors of your houses? They said: We did that intentionally so that we would not forget death, and its memory would not leave our hearts. He said: So why do your houses not have doors? They said: There is no one accused among us, and there is none among us who is not trustworthy and reliable. He said: So why is it that you have no rulers over you? They said: We do not wrong one another. He said: So why is it that you have no rulers among you? They said: We do not dispute. He said: So why is it that you have no rich people among you? They said: We do not compete with one another.

He said: So why is it that you have no kings among you? They said: We do not act arrogantly. He said: So why do you not dispute or differ? They said: Because our hearts are in harmony and our relations are sound. He said: So why do you not insult one another or fight one another? They said: Because we have overcome our natures with determination, and have governed ourselves with patience. He said: So why is your word one, and your path straight and level? They said: Because we do not lie to one another, nor deceive one another, nor backbite one another. He said: So tell me, how did your hearts become alike and your conduct become straight? They said: Our hearts are sound, and thus rancor and envy were removed from our hearts. He said: So why is it that there is no poor or needy person among you? They said: Before, we used to divide equally. He said: So why is there no rude or harsh person among you?

They said: Before, you were humble and modest. He said: So what made you the people with the longest lives? They said: Before, we used to deal with what is right and rule with justice. He said: So why are you not afflicted with drought? They said: We do not neglect to seek forgiveness. He said: So why are you not afflicted with hardship? They said: Before, we prepared ourselves for calamity since we were young, and we loved it and were keen on it, so we were stripped of it. He said: So why are calamities not befalling you as they befall people? They said: We do not trust in anyone but God, and we do not act according to the signs and stars. He said: Tell me, did you find your fathers doing this? They said: Yes, we found our fathers having mercy on their poor and comforting their needy, forgiving those who wronged them, being good to those who mistreated them, being patient with those who were ignorant of them, asking forgiveness for those who insulted them, maintaining family ties, fulfilling their trusts, preserving their time for prayer, fulfilling their promises, being truthful in their appointments, not turning away from their equals, and not being disdainful of their relatives.
So God put their affairs right for them and preserved them as long as they were alive, and it was God’s right to preserve them in their estate.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Rafi, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet of God,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Gog and Magog dig the dam every day, until they see the rays of the sun. Then God says: Go back and dig it tomorrow. Then God restores it to the state it was in when they left it. Then when the time comes, He says: God willing. So they dig it and come out to the people and dry up the water, and the people fortify themselves in their forts, and they throw their arrows towards the sky, and they return with them like blood, and they say: We have defeated the people of the earth, and we have overcome the people of the heaven. Then God sends upon them a scorpion in their necks and it kills them. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the beasts of the earth grow fat and thank God for their flesh. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Asim ibn Umar ibn Qatada al-Ansari then al-Dhafri, on Surat al-Kahf 18:94 They said, "O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are
h
corrupters in the land

. So may we assign you an expenditure on condition that you make between us and them a barrier?" the authority of Mahmud ibn Labid, the brother of Banu Abd al-Ashhal, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Gog and Magog will be conquered and will come out upon the people as God, the Almighty, has said. They will come down from every side and cover the earth. The Muslims will withdraw from them to their cities and fortresses, and they will gather their livestock with them and drink the waters of the earth.

x: Some of them will pass by a river and drink what is in it until they leave it dry.

Some of them will pass by that river and say: ‘There was water here once,’ until there is no one left among the people who has not withdrawn to a fortress or a city. One of them will say: ‘These are the people of the earth; we have finished with them. The people of heaven remain.’ Then one of them will shake his spear and throw it into the sky, and it will return to him covered in blood as a result of the affliction and tribulation. While they are on…” Then, God sent worms in their necks like mites, and they came out in their necks and they became dead, and no sound was heard from them. The Muslims said: Is there not a man who will sell himself for us, so he can see what the enemy has done? He said: So a man from them will strip himself for that, hoping for reward for himself, and he has prepared it for himself that he will be killed. So he goes down and finds them dead, one on top of the other, and he calls out: O group of Muslims?

Do not rejoice, for God has sufficed you against your enemy. So they come out of their cities and fortresses, and they let their livestock go out, and they have no grazing except their flesh, and they are grateful for them better than they are grateful for any plant they have ever eaten.

c: Bahr bin Nasr told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Muawiyah, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahariyyah and Shureih bin Ubaid: Gog and Magog are of three types: a type whose height is like the height of a cedar, a type whose height and width are the same, and a type whose ear is spread out and the other is covered so that it covers the rest of his body.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: They said, ‘O Dhul-Qarnayn, indeed Gog and Magog are
h
corrupters in the land

.’ He said: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri used to say: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Not a single one of them will die until a thousand men are born to his loins. He said: ʿAbdullah ibn Masʿud used to marvel at their great number and say: Not a single one of Gog and Magog will die until a thousand men are born to him from his loins. The report that we mentioned from Wahb bin Munabbih in the story of Gog and Magog indicates that those who said to Dhul-Qarnayn, Indeed, Gog and Magog are
h
corrupters in the land

, only informed him of their fear of what they would do of corruption in the land, not that they suspected any corruption from them in themselves or in others. The reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, are that they would cause corruption in the land, and there is no indication in them that they had caused corruption in the land before Dhul-Qarnayn created the barrier that he built between them and those other than them from the people. If that is the case with what we have explained, then the correct interpretation of his statement, Indeed, Gog and Magog are
h
corrupters in the land
, is that Gog and Magog will cause corruption in the land. And his statement,
h
Then shall we make for you a burden
? The reciters differed in their recitation of that, so most of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it,
h
Then shall we make for you a burden

? as if they had made it similar to the source of the root to go out of the head, and that is what they made it. The majority of Kufi readers read it as Falla nanja’il laka kharj with an alif, as if they had made it a noun, and meant by it a fee for your building a dam between us and these people. The first of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the correct reading of the one who reads it Fall we make nk kharaj with an alif, because the people, as has been reported about them, only offered Dhul-Qarnayn to give him from their wealth what would help him build the dam, and he explained that by saying So help me with strength, I will make between you and them a barrier, and they did not offer him a tribute on their heads. Kharaj among the Arabs is the yield. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we have said about that.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: Shall we give you a tax? He said: A reward, on condition that you make a barrier between us and them.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Shall We then make for you a tribute? He said: A wage.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, Then shall we make for you a tribute? He said: A wage. And his statement,
h
On condition that you place between us and them a barrier

? He said: They said to him: Shall we make for you a tribute until you place between us and Gog and Magog a barrier that will stand between us and them and prevent them from coming out to us? And it is the barrier.

evidence.text: The reciters differed in the reading of his saying, Indeed, Gog and Magog are corrupters in the land.

The reciters from the people of Hijaz, Iraq, and others read Indeed, Gog and Magog without a hamza on the basis of fa'ul from yajjat and majjat, and they made the two alifs in them extra, except for Asim bin Abi al-Najud and al-A'raj, for he mentioned that they read it with a hamza in both of them, and they made the hamza in them from the root of the speech, and it is as if they made Yajuj: yaf'ul from ajajat, and ma'juj: maf'ul.

The reading that is the correct reading according to us, is Indeed, Gog and Magog with an alif without a hamza, due to the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it, and that it is the well-known speech on the tongues of the Arabs, and from it is the saying of Ru'bah bin al-'Ajaj: If Gog and Magog were together, 'Ad would return and seek help from them, and they are two nations from behind the dam.

The reciters differed in their recitation of that, so most of the reciters of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa recited it, Then shall we make for you a burden? as if they had made it similar to the source of the root to go out of the head, and that is what they made it.
The majority of Kufi readers read it as Falla nanja’il laka kharj with an alif, as if they had made it a noun, and meant by it a fee for your building a dam between us and these people.

The first of the two readings in this regard, in our view, is the correct reading of the one who reads it Fall we make nk kharaj with an alif, because the people, as has been reported about them, only offered Dhul-Qarnayn to give him from their wealth what would help him build the dam, and he explained that by saying So help me with strength, I will make between you and them a barrier, and they did not offer him a tribute on their heads.

x: God Almighty says: Dhul-Qarnayn said: The one who enabled me to do what you asked me to do of the dam between you and these people is my Lord, and He made it easy for me and strengthened me over it. He is better than what you have made, and the wage that you offer me for building that is more and better, but help me from among you with strength, help me with work and craftsmen who are good at building and working.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: What my Lord has empowered me in is better, so help me with strength. He said: With men.
h
I will place between you and them a barrier
. He said: What He has empowered me in, so he assimilated one of the two noons into the other, but it is what He has empowered me in. And His saying:
h
I will place between you and them a barrier

means: I will place between you and Gog and Magog a barrier. And the barrier is the barrier of a wall and a dam, except that it is more impenetrable and stronger. It is said from it: So-and-so has blocked such-and-such a place, he blocks it with a block and a barrier. And it is also said: He blocked his garment and he blocks it, and it is a patched garment: if it has many patches, and from it is the saying of Antarah: Did the poets leave the ruins or did you know the house after the illusion? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Shall I place between you and them a barrier
? He said: It is like the strictest barrier.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said:
m: It was mentioned to us that a man said: O Prophet of God, I have seen the dam of Gog and Magog. He said: Describe it to me. He said: It is like ink-coloured hail, one path is black and the other is red. He said: I have seen it.

x: The Almighty says: Dhul-Qarnayn said to those who asked him to build a barrier between them and Gog and Magog, Bring me: meaning, bring me iron bars, which is the plural of zibra, and zibra is a piece of iron.

c: As Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying pieces of iron means: pieces of iron.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Bring me sheets of iron
, he said: pieces of iron.

c: Ismail bin Saif told me: Ali bin Mashair told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh,
m: regarding his statement, pieces of iron, he said: pieces of iron.

c: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ubaid God bin Musa told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Bring me sheets of iron
, he said: pieces of iron.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Bring me sheets of iron
: meaning split iron.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Bring me sheets of iron
, he said: pieces of iron.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said:
m: h
Bring me sheets of iron

. He said: pieces of iron. And His statement, Until, when he had leveled between the two mountain-sides, the Almighty says: So they brought him sheets of iron, and he placed them between the two mountain-sides until, when he had leveled between the two mountains with what he had placed between them of sheets of iron. It is said: he leveled. The two mountain-sides is what is between the sides of the two mountains and their tops, and from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: I took what was between the width of the two sides of the shells and the tops of the two corners. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.

x: Who said that?

c: Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement, between the two mountain-sides, meaning: between the two mountains.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Ait, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Until when he reached between the two mountains. He said: It was a mountain between two mountains. The two mountains are the two mountains.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa H told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement the two mountaintops means the tops of the two mountains.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement, between the two mountain ranges, meaning the two mountains, which are on the side of Armenia and Azerbaijan.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada:
m: Until when He made the two mountains level.

c: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Al-Qasim told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: that he read it as Bayn as-Sadafeen with the sad and dal in the accusative case, and he said: Bayn al-Jabalayn. The Arabs have three dialects for as-Sadafeen, and a group of reciters have read each of them: the fat-ha on the sad and the dal, which is the reading of the general reciters of the people of Medina and Kufa, the damma on both of them, which is the reading of the people of Basra, and the damma on the sad and the sukoon on the dal, which is the reading of some of the people of Mecca and Kufa. The fat-ha on the sad and the dal is the most famous of these dialects, and reading with them is more pleasing to me, although I permit reading with all of them, because their meanings are the same. I chose the fat-ha on Surat al-Kahf 18:96
h
Bring me sheets of iron

. Until, when he had leveled between the two mountain-shells, he said, "Blow." Until, when he had made it into fire, he said, "Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper." both of them for the reason I mentioned. And His statement, He said, ‘Blow,’ means, the Almighty said, He said to the doers: Blow the fire upon these iron plates. And his saying, Until when He made it a fire, and in the speech there is something omitted, which is: So they blew, until when He made what was between the two mountain-sides of iron a fire, “He said, ‘Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper,’” so the reciters differed in the recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it, He said, ‘Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper.

x: Some of the reciters of Kufa recited it, He said, ‘Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper, connecting the alif, meaning, bring me molten copper, as one says, I took the reins, and I took the reins, and I brought you Zayd, and I brought you Zayd. And the meaning of that, if it is recited in this way, may be directed to the meaning of give me, so it is as if the reciter wanted to extend the alif of Atooni, so he left out the first hamza of Atooni, and if the first is dropped, he hamzas the second. His saying,
h
Pour molten copper over him
, means:
h
pour molten copper over him
. Molten copper is the word used by the people of interpretation.
The scholars of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his statement,
h
Pour molten copper over him
, he said: The molten copper is copper.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding his statement,
h
Pour molten copper over it
: He meant copper.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
Pour molten copper over him
meaning copper to bind him with it.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
Pour molten copper over it
, he said: Copper.

i: Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language from Basra used to say: Molten iron is molten iron, and he supported his statement with the words of the poet:
x: Hasama is like the color of salt, its iron is pure, and its diameters are forbidden.

evidence.text: Ahmad bin Yusuf told me: Al-Qasim told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he read it as Bayn as-Sadafeen with the sad and dal in the accusative case, and he said: Bayn al-Jabalayn.

The Arabs have three dialects for as-Sadafeen, and a group of reciters have read each of them: the fat-ha on the sad and the dal, which is the reading of the general reciters of the people of Medina and Kufa, the damma on both of them, which is the reading of the people of Basra, and the damma on the sad and the sukoon on the dal, which is the reading of some of the people of Mecca and Kufa.

And his saying, Until when He made it a fire, and in the speech there is something omitted, which is: So they blew, until when He made what was between the two mountain-sides of iron a fire, “He said, ‘Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper,’” so the reciters differed in the recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the people of Kufa, recited it, He said, ‘Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper.

Some of the reciters of Kufa recited it, He said, ‘Bring me, that I may pour over it molten copper, connecting the alif, meaning, bring me molten copper, as one says, I took the reins, and I took the reins, and I brought you Zayd, and I brought you Zayd.

And the meaning of that, if it is recited in this way, may be directed to the meaning of give me, so it is as if the reciter wanted to extend the alif of Atooni, so he left out the first hamza of Atooni, and if the first is dropped, he hamzas the second.

x: And His statement,
h
And they were not able to climb it

, the Almighty says: Gog and Magog were not able to climb the barrier that Dhul-Qarnayn had made as a barrier between them and the people below them, so that they could go over it and descend from it to the people. It is said from this: So-and-so appeared above the house, meaning he climbed it, and from this is the saying of the al-Nas 114:So-and-so appeared over so-and-so, meaning he overcame him and overcame him. And
h
they were not able to
tunnel through it, meaning: and
h
they were not able to
tunnel through it from below. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about this.
Mention of those who said this:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement, And
h
they were not able to
make it pass from above it, And
h
they were not able to
tunnel into it: meaning from below it.

c: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement, And
h
they were not able to
bring it forth, he said:
h
They were not able to
remove it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And they were not able to climb it
. He said: And
h
they were not able to
tunnel through it.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: And
h
they were not able to
ascend it, he said: nor were they able to tunnel through it. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj said:
h
They were not able to
ascend it. He said:
h
They were not able to
dig a tunnel for it. The Arab scholars differed about the reason for deleting the ta’ from his statement
h
They were not able to

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: He did that because the language of the Arabs is to say: ista’a yasti’, meaning: ista’a yastu’, but they deleted the ta’ when it is combined with the ta’ and their articulation point is the same. He said: Some of them said: ista’a, so the ta’ was deleted for that reason.
Some of them said: ista’a yasti’, so he made it from the qata’ as if it were ata’a yati’, so he made the seen a substitute for the sukoon of the waw.
Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: This is a letter that was used so often that it was deleted.

The Almighty says: When Dhul-Qarnayn saw that Gog and Magog could not expose what he had built of the rubble, nor could they dig through it, he said: This that I have built and leveled as a barrier between this nation and what is beyond the rubble is a mercy from my Lord with which He has shown mercy to those people beyond the rubble. He helped me with His mercy towards them until I built it and leveled it so that He might thereby avert the calamity of this nation from them. And His statement, Filled, then when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level, means: So when the promise of my Lord comes, which He has made a time for the emergence of this nation and their emergence from behind this rubble for them, He will make it level, meaning: He will level it with the ground, so He made it adhere to it from their saying: A she-camel with a flat back: one with a flat back and no hump.
The meaning of mark is: He made it level, so it was said: level.
And Qatadah used to say about that what:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement,
h
So when the promise of my Lord comes to pass

, He will make it level, he said: I do not know whether he meant the two mountains, or what is between them. And he mentioned that this will be the case after Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him, kills the Antichrist. The report mentioned that:

c: Ahmad bin Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi told me: Hisham bin Bashir told us: Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Jabalah bin Suhaim, on the authority of Muathir,
m: who is Ibn Afara, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “On the Night of the Isra’, I met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, and they discussed the matter of the Hour, and they referred the matter to Abraham. Abraham said: I have no knowledge of it, so they referred the matter to Moses. Moses said: I have no knowledge of it, so they referred the matter to Jesus. Jesus said: As for the establishment of the Hour, only God knows it, but my Lord has enjoined upon me what will happen before its time. He enjoined upon me that the Antichrist will emerge, and that he will be my destination. He mentioned that he has two reeds with him, and when he sees me, God will destroy him. He said: He will melt as lead melts, Hatter. Indeed, the stone and the tree will say: O Muslim, this is an infidel, so kill him, so God will destroy them, and the people will return to their lands and homelands, and Gog and Magog will meet them from every hill, swarming, and they will not come upon anything except that they will eat it.” They do not pass by any water but they drink it. People will return to them and complain about them. Then they will call upon God to kill them until the earth is dry from the stench of their stench. Then rain will come down and carry their bodies and throw them into the sea. Then the mountains will be blown away until the earth is like leather. So God has promised them that if that is the case, then the Hour will be like a pregnant woman whose family does not know when she will surprise them with her birth, by night or by day.

c: Ubayd ibn Ismail told me: Al-Muharibi told us, on the authority of Asba’ ibn Zayd, on the authority of Al-Awam ibn Hawshab, on the authority of Jabalah ibn Suhaim, on the authority of Muthathir ibn Affara, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, who said:
m: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he met with Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, peace be upon them. They discussed the matter of the Hour, and he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Ibrahim Al-Dawraqi on the authority of Hisham, and he added to it: Al-Awam ibn Hawshab said: I found confirmation of that in the Book of God, the Most High, God the Almighty said: Until, when Gog and Magog are let loose, and they rush from every height, * And the true promise draws near, and at once the eyes of those who disbelieved will stare in horror. And He said: But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will make it level, and ever has the promise of my Lord been true. He said: And the promise of my Lord, which He promised to my brethren in leveling this rubble, and the coming out of these people upon the people, and their wreaking havoc in it, and other than that of His promise, was true, because He does not break His promise, so nothing will happen except what He promised would happen.

x: God Almighty says: And We will leave Our servants on the Day when Our promise comes to them, which We promised them, that We will crush the mountains and blow them away from the earth with a blast, and We will leave it as a level plain, some of them surging into others. He says: Their jinn will mix with their humans.

c: Ibn Hamid narrated to us, saying: Yaqub al-Qummi narrated to us, on the authority of Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of a sheikh from Banu Fazara,
m: regarding His statement, And We will let some of them surge against others on that Day, he said: When the jinn and mankind surge, Iblis will say: I will teach you knowledge of this matter. So he will set out to the east and find that the angels have cut through the earth. Then he will set out to the west and find that the angels have cut through the earth. Then he will ascend right and left to the farthest reaches of the earth and find that the angels have cut through the earth. He will say: There is no escape. While he is like that, a path appears to him like a trap, so he and his offspring are seized by it. While they are on it, they attack the Fire, so God brings out a keeper from the keeper of the Fire, who will say: O Iblis, did you not have a position with your Lord, were you not in Paradise? He will say: This is not a day of reproach. If God had imposed on me an obligation, I would have worshipped Him in it in a way that no one else among His creation has worshipped Him in. He will say: Then God has imposed on you an obligation. He will say: What is it? He will say: He commands you to enter the Fire. So he will hesitate over it, and it will raise it and its offspring with its wings, and throw them into the Fire. The Fire will sigh a sigh, and there will not remain a close angel or a sent prophet except that it will kneel on its knees.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We will leave some of them that Day surging against others, he said: This is the beginning of the Resurrection, then the Trumpet will be blown, after that, and We will gather them together. And the Trumpet will be blown. We have already mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding the Trumpet, what it is, and what is meant by it. We have chosen the correct statement regarding that with its evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. However, we will mention in this place some of the reports that we did not mention in that place.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father: Aslam told us, on the authority of Bishr bin Shaghaf, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, that an Arab asked him about the trumpet. He said: A horn that blows.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Muawiyah bin Hisham told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Sulayman al-Taymi, on the authority of al-Ajli, on the authority of Bishr bin Shaghaf, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Muhammad ibn al-Harith al-Qantari narrated: Yahya ibn Abi Bakr narrated: I was at the funeral of Umar ibn Dhir and I met Malik ibn Mughul, who narrated to us on the authority of Atiyyah al-Awfi, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How do we know when the one with the horn has placed his head on the ground, bent his forehead, and lowered his ear, asking when he will be given the command? This was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he said: Say: God is sufficient for us, and in God we trust. If the people of Mina had gathered together, they would not have said that horn. So he said, but it is what they said.

c: Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Hafs told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can I enjoy myself when the companion of the horn has swallowed the horn, bent his back, and bulged his eyes? They said: What should we say, O Messenger of God? He said: Say: God is sufficient for us, we trust in God.

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can I enjoy myself while the owner of the horn has taken hold of the horn and bent his forehead, listening to when he is commanded to blow into it? The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: How can we say? He said: You say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. We trust in God.

c: Abu Kuraib and Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of Mutraf, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, the same.

c: Yaqub told me, he said: Shuʿayb ibn Harb told us, he said: Khalid Abu al-ʿAlaʿ told us, he said: ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi told us, on the authority of Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, he said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How can I enjoy myself while the companion of the horn has taken hold of the horn, bent his forehead, and is listening with his ear when he is commanded to blow? If the people of Mina were to gather around the horn to lift it from the ground, they would not be able to do so. He said: So the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were in despair, and it was difficult for them. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Say: God is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In God we trust. Abu Kuraib narrated: Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Maharibi narrated to us, on the authority of Ismail ibn Rafir al-Madani, on the authority of Yazid ibn so-and-so, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When God finished creating the heavens and the earth, He created the trumpet and gave it to Israfil, who placed it on his mouth, his gaze fixed on the Throne, waiting for when he would be commanded. Abu Hurayrah said: O Messenger of God, what is the trumpet? He said: A horn. He said: How is it? He said: A great horn in which three blasts will be blown: the first is the blast of terror, the second is the blast of unconsciousness, and the third is the blast of rising before the Lord of the Worlds. And His saying,
h
Then We gathered them together
, means that We gathered all of creation at that time for the place of reckoning, all together.

x: And His statement,
h
And We will present Hell that Day to the disbelievers

, plainly, means: And We will bring Hell to light on the Day the Trumpet is blown, so We will show it to the disbelievers in God, so that they may see it and witness it like a mirage. If the action were attributed to it, it would be said: It was presented if it became clear, as Amr ibn Kalghum said: And the dove turned away and haughtily bowed like swords in the hands of our sword-wielders. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar narrated: Abdur-Rahman bin Mahdi narrated: Sufyan narrated: Salamah Bara Kuhail narrated: Abu Az-Zura’ narrated: Abdullah said: The creation will stand for God when the Trumpet is blown, as one man. God, the Almighty, will appear to the creation, and no one who worshipped anything besides God will meet Him except that it will be raised up to him and follow him. He said: Then he will meet the Jews and say: Who do you worship? They will say: We worship Ezra. He said: Then he will say: Does water please you? They will say: Yes. Then he will show them Hell, and it will be like a mirage.
And We will present Hell, that Day, to the disbelievers, plainly.

Then he will meet the Christians and say: Who do you worship? They will say: We worship the Messiah. He will say: Does water please you? They will say: Yes. He will show them Hell, and it will be like a mirage. Then likewise for those who worshipped anything besides God.
Stop them, for they will be questioned.

God the Almighty says: And We shall present Hell on that Day to the disbelievers who did not look at the signs of God, nor ponder them, nor reflect upon His proofs, nor take heed from them, nor remember, nor turn to the Oneness of God, nor submit to His commands and prohibitions, but they were unable to hear, He says: And they were unable to hear the remembrance of God which He reminded them of, and His explanation which He made clear to them in His Book, due to God’s abandonment of them, and the overpowering of misery upon them, and their preoccupation with disbelief in God and obedience to Satan, so that they would learn from it, and ponder it, and know guidance from misguidance, and disbelief from faith.
And Mujahid used to say about that what:

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us,
m: all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement,
h
They are unable to hear
, he said: They are not able to understand.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: And they were unable to hear, he said: They did not know.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement,
h
Those whose eyes are covered from My remembrance
, he said: These are the people of disbelief.

x: The Almighty says: Do those who disbelieve in God, from the worshippers of angels and the Messiah, think that they can take My servants whom they worshipped instead of God as allies? He says: No, rather they are their enemies. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Mention the one who said to you:

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj,
m: regarding His statement,
h
Do those who disbelieve think that they can take My servants as allies other than Me

? He said: He means those who worship the Messiah, son of Mary, and the angels, and they are the servants of God, and they are not allies of the disbelievers. And with this reading, I mean with a kasra on the seen of af-hasab meaning to think, this is the reading of the readers of the regions. And it was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Ikrimah and Mujahid that they read it as Af-hasab those who disbelieve with a sukoon on the seen and raising the letter after it, meaning: Do they think that? That is, is it sufficient for them to take My servants as allies other than Me from My worship and loyalty? It was also narrated on the authority of Ishaq bin Yusuf al-Azraq, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Ikrimah, Do those who disbelieve think? He said: Do they think that? And the reading that we recite is the reading that the reciters of the regions follow. Do those who disbelieve think? with a kasra on the seen, meaning do they think, because of the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it. And His statement, Indeed, We have prepared Hell as a dwelling for the disbelievers, means: We have prepared Hell as a dwelling for those who disbelieve in God.

evidence.text: And with this reading, I mean with a kasra on the seen of af-hasab meaning to think, this is the reading of the readers of the regions.

And it was narrated on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, and Ikrimah and Mujahid that they read it as Af-hasab those who disbelieve with a sukoon on the seen and raising the letter after it, meaning: Do they think that?
And the reading that we recite is the reading that the reciters of the regions follow.
Do those who disbelieve think? with a kasra on the seen, meaning do they think, because of the consensus of the proof from the reciters on it.

x: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who seek to cause you trouble and argue with you falsely, and debate with you about issues from among the People of the Book: the Jews and the Christians, Shall We inform you, O people, who will be the greatest losers in [their] deeds? He means those who exhaust themselves in work seeking profit and excellence, but they attained ruin and destruction and did not attain what they sought, like the buyer of a commodity hoping for excellence and profit, but his hope was disappointed, and his sale was lost, and he was disappointed in what he hoped for.
The people of interpretation differed about those meant by that, and some of them said: It meant the monks and priests.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Maqburi told us: Haywah ibn Shureih told us: Al-Sakn ibn Abi Karimah told me that his mother told him that
m: she heard Abu Khamisah Abdullah ibn Qais say: I heard Ali ibn Abi Talib say about this verse: “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?” They are the monks who confined themselves to monasteries.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said:
m: I heard Haywah say: Al-Sakn bin Abi Karima told me, on the authority of his mother, she told him that she heard Abdullah bin Qais say: I heard Ali bin Abi Talib say, and he mentioned something similar.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal ibn Yasaf, on the authority of Musʿab ibn Saʿd, he said:
m: I said to my father, And they think that they are doing good are they the Kharijites? He said: They are the people of the monasteries.

c: Fadala bin Al-Fadl told us: Buzay’ said:
m: A man asked Al-Dahhak about this verse: “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?” He said: They are the priests and monks.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, on the authority of Musʿab bin Saʿd, who said: Saʿd said:
m: They are the owners of the monasteries.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibn Saad, who said:
m: I said to Saad: O my father, Shall we inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds? Are they the Kharijites? He said: No, but they are the people of the monasteries. However, the Kharijites are a people who have deviated, so God has made their hearts deviate.

x: Others said: Rather, they are all the People of the Two Books.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us: Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of ʿAmr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Musʿab ibn Saʿd, who said:
m: I asked my father about this verse: “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers as to [their] deeds? Those whose effort is lost in worldly life.” Are they the Kharijites? He said: No, they are the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. As for the Jews, they denied Muhammad. As for the Christians, they disbelieved in Paradise and said: There is no food or drink in it. But the Kharijites are “those who break the covenant of God after its ratification and sever that which God has ordered to be joined and spread corruption on earth. It is those who are the losers.” So Saʿd used to call them the wicked.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Abi Hurriyah, on the authority of Musʿab bin Saʿd bin Abi Waqqas, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement, Say, ‘Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?’ He said: They are the Jews and the Christians. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Abu Harb ibn Abi Al-Aswad narrated: Zadhan narrated: Ali ibn Abi Talib was asked about the statement of God, “Say: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?” He said: They are the disbelievers among the People of the Book, as if their forefathers were on the right path, but they associated partners with their Lord and innovated in their religion. They strive in falsehood, thinking that they are on the right path, and strive in misguidance, thinking that they are on the right path. Their efforts are in the life of this world, while they think that they are doing good. Then he raised his voice and said: The people of Hell are not far from them.

x: Others said: Rather, they are the Khawarij.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Salamah, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, who said:
m: Abdullah bin al-Kawwa asked Ali about his statement, Say, ‘Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds?’ He said: You, O people of Harura.

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yahya ibn Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Sakhr, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah al-Bajali, on the authority of Abu al-Sahbaa al-Bakri, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib,
m: that Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about the statement of God Almighty: Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in [their] deeds? Ali said: You and your companions.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Salamah bin Kuhail, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyal, who said:
m: Ibn al-Kawwa’ stood up to Ali and said: Who are the greatest losers in their deeds? Are their efforts wasted in this worldly life, while they think that they are doing well? He said: Woe to you, the people of Harura are among them.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn Uthmah told us: Musa ibn Yaqub ibn Abdullah told us: Abu al-Huwayrith told us, on the authority of Nafi’ ibn Jubayr ibn Mut’im:
m: Ibn al-Kawwa’ said to Ali ibn Abi Talib: Who are the greatest losers in their deeds, those whose efforts have been wasted in the life of this world? He said: You and your companions. The correct statement in this regard, according to us, is to say that God, the Almighty, meant by His statement, Shall We inform you of the greatest losers in their deeds? every doer of a deed who thinks he is right in it, and that by doing that he is obedient and pleasing to God, but by doing that he is displeased with God, and is unjust in his path to the people of faith in Him, such as monks, deacons, and their likes from the people of ijtihad in their misguidance, and despite that, by their actions and their striving for God, they are disbelievers, regardless of the people of religion they are. The Arabists differed about the reason for the accusative case of his statement deeds.

x: Some of the grammarians of Basra said: It is accusative because Surat al-Kahf 18:104 Those whose efforts are wasted in worldly life, while they think that they are doing well in work. when he introduced the alif, lam, and nun in al-akhsarin, it did not lead to the addition, and the deeds were from al-akhsarin, so that is why it is accusative.

Another said: This is the chapter on af'al and fa'l, like al-afdal and al-fadla, and al-akhsar and al-khusra, and the waw does not enter into it, and there is no explanatory word in it, because it is separated by what it is like in his statement al-afdal and al-fadla, and if an explanatory word comes with it, it is for the first and the last. He said: Do you not see that you say: I passed by a man with a handsome face, so the handsomeness is for the man and the face, and likewise great in mind, and the like? He said: It is permissible in al-akhsarin because he returned it to af'al and af'ala. He said: I heard the Arabs say: the first ones enter, and the last ones exit, so it became for the first and the second like the rest of the chapter. He said: And this is how it is measured. And His statement,
h
Those whose effort is lost in the life of this world

, means: They are those whose work that they did in their life of this world was not based on guidance and righteousness, but rather was based on injustice and misguidance, and that is because they did not do what God commanded them to do, but rather on their disbelief in Him, and they think that they are doing good work, meaning: They think that by doing that for God, they are obedient, and striving in what He has urged His servants to do.

This is one of the clearest proofs of the error of the statement of those who claim that no one disbelieves in God except when he intends to disbelieve after the name of His Oneness, and that is because God, the Most High, mentioned, informed about those whose description He described in this verse, that their effort that they strove in this world was lost, and they thought that they were doing good in that work, and He informed about them that they are the ones who disbelieved in the signs of their Lord. And if the statement were as those who claimed that no one disbelieves in God except when he knows, then it would be necessary that these people would be rewarded for their work, which God informed about them that they thought that they were doing good work. They will be rewarded for it, but the statement is contrary to what they said.

c: God Almighty informed us
m: about them that they are disbelievers in God and that their deeds are in vain. He meant by His statement that they do good work work, and workmanship, craftsmanship, and manufacturing are one and the same. It is said: a horse is made, meaning manufactured.

x: God the Almighty says: These are the ones whose characteristics We have described, the greatest losers in their deeds, those who disbelieved in the proofs and evidence of their Lord, and denied meeting Him. So their deeds have become worthless. He says: Their deeds have become worthless, so they have no reward that will benefit their owners in the Hereafter, but rather they will have a long torment and disgrace from them. So We will not assign to them any weight on the Day of Resurrection. God the Almighty says: So We will not assign to them any weight. What He meant by that is that their scales will not be heavy because the scales are only weighed down by righteous deeds, and these people have no righteous deeds that would make their scales heavy. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Shammar, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Ka’b, who said:
m: A great, tall man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, but he will not weigh as much as a mosquito’s wing in God’s sight. Recite: So We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Ibn Al-Salt told us, he said: Ibn Abi Al-Zinad told us, on the authority of Salih,
m: the freedman of Al-Taw’amah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God said: The glutton, the drinker, the tall one will be brought and weighed, but he will not weigh as much as the wing of a mosquito. Then he recited: So We will not assign to them on the Day of Resurrection any weight.

x: God Almighty says: Their reward is Hell for their disbelief in God, their mockery of the verses of His Book and the arguments of His Messengers, and their ridicule of His Messengers.

God Almighty says: Indeed, those who believed in God and His Messenger, and acknowledged the oneness of God and what He revealed of His books and acted in obedience to Him, will have the gardens of Paradise. Paradise is the largest part of Paradise, as Umayyah said: Their homes at that time were evident in them the gardens, the foman, and the onions.
The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of Paradise.
Some of them said: It means the best and middle of Paradise.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abbas bin Al-Waleed told us: Yazid bin Zari’ told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, who said:
m: Al-Firdaws is the highest part of Paradise, its middle and best part.

c: Ahmad bin Abi Sarij Al-Razi told us: Al-Haitham Abu Bishr told us: Al-Faraj bin Fadala told us, on the authority of Lasman, on the authority of Amer, who said:
m: Abu Usama was asked about Al-Firdaws, and he said: It is the navel of Paradise. Ahmad bin Abi Surayj said:

c: Hammad bin Amr Al-Nusaybi told us, on the authority of Abu Ali, on the authority of Ka’b, who said:
m: There is no higher paradise in Paradise than the Paradise of Firdaws, and in it are those who enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong.

x: Others said: It is the garden in Roman.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ali bin Sahl al-Ramli told me: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: Al-Firdaws is a garden in Roman.

c: Al-Abbas bin Muhammad told us: Hajjaj told us: Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah told me, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

x: Others said: It is the garden in which there are grapes.
Who said that?

c: Abbas bin Muhammad told us, he said:
m: Muhammad bin Ubaid, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Yazid bin Abi Ziyad, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Ka’b, he said: The gardens of Paradise in which there are grapes. The correct thing to say about this is what the hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, have shown. This is what: Ahmad bin Abi narrated to us, saying:

c: Yazid bin Harun narrated to us, saying: Hammam bin Yahya narrated to us, saying: Zaid bin Aslam narrated to us, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Paradise has one hundred levels, between each two levels is a year’s journey, and al-Firdaws is the highest level of it, and from it are the four rivers, and al-Firdaws is above them, so if you ask God, ask Him for al-Firdaws.

c: Musa bin Sahl told us: Musa bin Dawud told us: Hammam bin Yahya told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Ubadah bin al-Samit,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Paradise has one hundred levels, between each two levels is like the distance between the sky and the earth. The highest of them is al-Firdaws, and from it the four rivers of Paradise boast. So if you ask God for something, ask Him for al-Firdaws.”

c: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Yahya bin Sulayman told me, on the authority of Hilal bin Usamah, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah,
m: or Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: If you ask God, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle of Paradise and the highest part of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, Blessed and Exalted be He, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Amer told us, he said: Falih told us, on the authority of Hilal, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abi Umrah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet,
m: may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly, except that he said: The middle of Paradise. He also said: (And from it gushes forth or gushes forth.

c: Ammar bin Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me: Yahya bin Saleh told us: Abdul Aziz bin Muhammad told us: Zaid bin Aslam told us, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Muadh bin Jabal,
m: that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: In Paradise there are one hundred levels, between each two levels is like the distance between the sky and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the highest and middle of Paradise, and above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful, and from it flow the rivers of Paradise. So if you ask God for something, ask Him for Al-Firdaws.

c: Ahmad bin Mansour told us: Abd al-Samad bin Abd al-Warith told us: al-Harith bin Umair told us, on the authority of his father, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The Gardens of Paradise are four, two of them are made of gold, their ornaments and their vessels, and whatever is in them, and two of them are made of silver, their ornaments and their vessels, and whatever Surat al-Kahf 18:107 Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging. is in them.

c: Ahmad bin Abi Surayj told us: Abu Naim told us: Abu Qudamah told us, on the authority of Abu Imran al-Joni, on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abdullah bin Qais, on the authority of his father, who said: The Messenger of God said:
m: The Gardens of Paradise are four: two of gold, their ornaments, their vessels, and what is in them, and two of silver, their ornaments, their vessels, and what is in them.

c: Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs, on the authority of Shammar, who said:
m: God created the Garden of Paradise with His own hand, and He opens it every Thursday, saying: Increase in goodness for My friends, increase in beauty for My friends.

c: Ibn al-Barqi told us: Ibn Abi Maryam told us: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ibn al-Darawardi told us: Zayd ibn Aslam told us, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ ibn Yasar, on the authority of Muʿadh ibn Jabal, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Paradise has one hundred levels, each level as far as the distance between heaven and earth, and the highest level among them is al-Firdaws.

c: Ahmad bin Yahya al-Sufi told me: Ahmad bin al-Faraj al-Ta’if told us: al-Walid bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Bashir, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of Samra bin, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Al-Firdaws is a hill in Paradise, it is its middle and most beautiful part.

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Udayqi told us: Ismail bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Samurah bin Jundub, who said:
m: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told us: Al-Firdaws is the highest, most beautiful, and most elevated part of Paradise.

c: Muhammad bin Marzouq told me: Rawh bin Ubadah told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik,
m: that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Ar-Rabi’ bint An-Nadr: O Umm Haritha, these are gardens, and your son has attained the highest Paradise. Paradise is the highest part of Paradise, its middle and best part. His statement, a place of residence, means homes and dwellings. Home comes from nuzul, which is from the descent of some people upon others. As for nuzul, it is the rent. It is said, There is no place of residence for this food of yours, meaning the rent. And we did not find a place of residence with you, meaning a place of residence.

x: And his saying, Immortal means: abiding therein forever. They do not desire to move from it means: they do not desire to change from it. It is the source of the verb to move, which was taken back to its original form, just as it is said: to be small means to become small, and to be crooked means to be crooked. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us
And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us
m: both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, They do not desire to change from it. He said: To change.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: something similar.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said:
m: I heard Mukhallad bin Al-Hussein say, and he was asked about it, he said: I heard some of the companions of Anas say: He said: The first of them to enter says: God only let me enter first, because there is no one better than me, and the last of them to enter says: God only delayed me, because there is no one to whom God has given like what He has given me.

x: The Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad: “If the sea were ink for the pen with which He writes the words of my Lord, the water of the sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We were to bring the like of it as a supplement.” He says: Even if We were to replenish the sea with the like of what is in it of water, as a supplement, from the saying of the one who says: I have come to you as a supplement for you, and that is from the meaning of increase. And it has been mentioned from some of them: And if We were to bring the like of it as a supplement, the reader of that was like that, meaning: The sea would be exhausted before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even if We were to add the like of what is in it of the ink with which He writes as ink. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said:
m: Isa H. A., and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement
h
The sea is ink for the words of my Lord refers to the pen

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: the same.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: his statement,
h
If the sea were ink for the words of my Lord
, meaning: Then the water of the sea would run out before the words and judgment of God run out.

x: God Almighty says: Say to these polytheists, O Muhammad: I am only a human being like you, from the children of Adam. I have no knowledge except what God has taught me. God has revealed to me that your God, whom you must worship and not associate anything with, is One God, with no second or partner. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord means: whoever fears his Lord on the Day of Meeting Him, and watches Him for his sins, and hopes for His reward for his obedience, let him do righteous work means: let him devote his worship to Him, and single out Him for divinity. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ ibn Abi Rashid, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr:
m: So whoever hopes to meet his Lord he said: the reward of his Lord. And His statement:
h
And associate no one with the worship of his Lord

means: and does not make for Him a partner in his worship of Him. Rather, he would be making for Him a partner in his worship if he shows off with his action which appears to be for God, but he intends by it someone other than Him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.

x: Who said that?

c: Abu Kuraib told us: Amr ibn Ubayd told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: And he does not associate anyone with the worship of his Lord.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us,
m: And he does not associate anyone with the worship of his Lord. He said: He does not show off.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, on the authority of Tawus, who said:
m: A man came and said: O Prophet of God, I love jihad in the way of God, and I love for him to see my homeland and for him to see my place. So God Almighty revealed: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid and Muslim bin Khalid Al-Zanji, on the authority of Sadaqah bin Yasar, he said:
m: A man came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and mentioned something similar, and he added to it: I do the work and give charity and I love for people to see it, and the rest of the hadith is similar to it.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Isa bin Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, he said:
m: Hamza Abu Amara, the client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, he said: A man came to Ubadah bin As-Samit and asked him, saying: Tell me about what I am asking you about. Have you seen a man who prays seeking the face of God and loves to be praised, and fasts seeking the face of God and loves to be praised? Ubadah said: He has nothing, for God, the Almighty, the Majestic, says: I am the best partner, so whoever has a partner with Me, then it is all his, I have no need of him.

c: Abu Amir Ismail bin Amr Al-Sakuni told us, he said, Hisham bin Ammar told us, he said: Ibn Ayyash told us, he said: Amr bin Qais Al-Kindi told us, that
m: he heard Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan recite this verse: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone. And he said: It is the last verse revealed from the Qur’an. Surat al-Kahf 18:110 Say, "I am only a human being like you. It has been revealed to me that your God is one God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone."

evidence.text: Abu Amir Ismail bin Amr Al-Sakuni told us, he said, Hisham bin Ammar told us, he said: Ibn Ayyash told us, he said: Amr bin Qais Al-Kindi told us, that he heard Muawiyah bin Abi Sufyan recite this verse: So whoever hopes for the meeting with his Lord - let him do righteous work and not associate in the worship of his Lord anyone.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/212 to Ibn Abī Shayba and Ibn al-Mundhir. It is in Tafsīr ʿAbd al-Razzāq 1/396, 397 from Maʿmar, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, without “from Mujāhid”. Ibn Kathīr mentions it in his Tafsīr 5/135 from Mujāhid, with “their building” (kāna bunyānuhum) in place of “the book of their exposition” (kitāb tibyānihim).
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 4/ 212 إلى ابن أبي شيبة وابن المنذر، وهو في تفسير عبد الرزاق 1/ 396، 397 عن معمر، عن ابن أبي نجيح، ليس فيه: عن مجاهد. وذكره ابن كثير في تفسيره 5/ 135 عن مجاهد، وفيه: كان بنيانهم. بدلا من: كتاب تبيانهم.

notes.en: Al-Suyūṭī attributes it in al-Durr al-manthūr 4/211 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim, limited to its beginning; Ibn Kathīr mentions it in full in his Tafsīr 5/135.

The adopted form is as will come in some of the manuscripts and in the two sources of the takhrīj and in the general run of history books. See al-Kāmil 1/355, al-Muntaẓam 2/152, 153, and al-Bidāya wa-l-nihāya 2/563.
